League One

Will Leicester turn things around?

Image: Leicester City manager Russell Martin

For just the second time in their history, and just 10 years after they won the Premier League title, Leicester City have found themselves in League One.

Russell Martin has taken the helm, as they look to end a miserable run of back-to-back relegations. He also has work to do in winning over some doubters, after miserable ends to his spells at Southampton and Rangers in his last two roles.

The addition of experience has been the aim of the summer, with the likes of Liam Cullen, Conor Chaplin and Wes Burns already joining.

A new dawn for Wednesday and who else could compete for promotion?

The Chansiri era is finally over at Sheffield Wednesday, and there has been a swirl of optimism around the club under new owner David Storch, despite relegation.

Henrik Pedersen, who led the Owls through the grim 2025/26 season, has been given the opportunity to see if he can get more out of a squad that is actually built to compete.

Louie Barry is an eye-catching addition. Injuries have blighted his progress but he has shown what a star he can be at this level for Stockport County, while Barry Bannan is back home after his stint at Millwall.

Luton are quite fancied under Jack Wilshere after a positive run in the second half of last season.

As are Plymouth Argyle, who have been exceptional so far in 2026, just missing out on the play-offs.

Managerial changes in League One

Image: Aaron Ramsey has taken his first permanent managerial role at Oxford United

There has been a particularly notable appointment at Oxford United, with Aaron Ramsey taking his first permanent managerial role to replace Matt Bloomfield, who surprisingly departed in the summer.

It has not been an easy start for Ramsey, however, as he has already had to deal with a transfer embargo which has left him unable to make any additions at the relegated club.

Elsewhere, Daniel Stendel has returned to Barnsley, Martin Drury has taken charge at Huddersfield Town and Jimmy McNulty left Rochdale to join Stockport following the departure of Dave Challinor.

Bromley's first season in the third tier!

Bromley were promoted to the EFL for the first time in their history in 2024, and it took just two seasons for them to seal promotion from League Two.

The Ravens won the title last season, and will now compete in the third tier of English football for the first time. It has only been 11 years since they were promoted to the National League for the first time.

They have been installed as the favourites for relegation, but Andy Woodman's side have defied the critics before and will be keen to do so again. Don't rule out anything at Hayes Lane.

League Two

All change at York and Rochdale

Image: Scott Lindsey has been appointed at York City

After 10 years away, York City are back in the EFL!

But it has not been all smooth sailing since. A couple of weeks before the start of the season, manager Stuart Maynard - who led them to promotion with more than 100 points - departed the club.

His replacement Scott Lindsey has not proven popular so far. In his first game in charge York exited the Carabao Cup at the preliminary phase, with fans booing and calling for the return of Maynard.

Not quite the return the Minstermen would have wanted to League Two.

The side they edged to automatic promotion in the National League, Rochdale, have also lost their manager after fighting their way through the play-offs.

McNulty moved on to Stockport, and they have dipped into non-League to appoint their new manager, with Ian Watson joining from National League North side South Shields.

Will Salford City finally get over the line?

Image: Macaulay Langstaff is one of the summer arrivals at Salford City

It is seven years now since Salford City were promoted to League Two, and still they have not managed to get over the line.

Last season was the closest they have come, losing in the play-off final to Notts County. Manager Karl Robinson has since departed, with Peter Cklamovski taking his place, having most recently been in charge of the Malaysia national side.

They have gone big in the transfer market, too. Macaulay Langstaff and Luke Molyneux have already arrived. Could this be the year the club owned by Gary Neville and David Beckham finally reach League One?

Managerial changes in League Two

Elsewhere, there are a lot of new managers to keep an eye on. Chris Hogg has come in at Northampton Town, while another relegated club in Rotherham United have appointed Alex Bruce.

Darrell Clarke takes charge at Tranmere Rovers, Lee Grant is at Walsall and Hayden Mullins will lead Newport County this season.

Sports.title: Sky Sports agrees deal to show Laver Cup from London's O2 in September
Sports.content:
Sky Sports has agreed a deal with Trident8 to show all three days of the Laver Cup from London's O2 arena this September, as 12 of the world's best men's players compete in the annual Europe vs 'Rest of the World' showdown.

World No 2 Carlos Alcaraz and Wimbledon finalist Alexander Zverev will be in action for Team Europe, while USA pair Ben Shelton and Taylor Fritz will lead the charge for Team World under the stewardship of captain Andre Agassi.

Hosted by presenter Gigi Salmon, Sky Sports will broadcast all 12 matches across day and night sessions on Friday September 25 and Saturday September 26, followed by a single concluding session on Sunday September 27. There will also be a reporter on the ground keeping fans abreast of all the news from the weekend's action.

Alongside broadcast rights, fans in the UK and Ireland will also be able to catch up on all the action with clips and highlights available across Sky's digital and social platforms.

Team Europe vice-captain and Sky Sports Tennis expert Tim Henman said: "It's great news the Laver Cup will be on Sky Sports.

"It's a unique opportunity to see the best players in the world coming together to represent Team Europe and Team World at the iconic O2 arena.

"Fans can expect plenty of drama, passion and rivalry, both on and off the court."

Live tennis is available all year on Sky Sports, including the Cincinnati Open beginning on Thursday August 13 and the US Open from Sunday August 30.

Sky Sports will broadcast over 4,000 matches and 80 tournaments this season, which are also available to stream with NOW and the Sky Sports app.

Sports.title: Jodar on course for tennis history as Rybakina fights past Osaka
Sports.content:
Spanish teenager Rafael Jodar is on course to break the record for the fastest rise into the top 10 of men's tennis after beating Arthur Filis in the quarter-finals of the Canadian Open.

Jodar came out on top in a rain-affected contest on Tuesday to win 7-6 (7-5) 6-3 to ensure he will move up to at least 11th in the ATP rankings, having started the year in 165th.

The 19-year-old will face American Brandon Nakashima in the semi-finals on Wednesday night, live on Sky Sports Tennis, where victory could see him smash Boris Becker's current record of 210 days to go from breaking the top 100 to being in the top 10. Jodar would do it in just 140 days.

However, Jodar also requires defending Canadian Open champion Ben Shelton to lose to Learner Tien in the other semi-final.

Shelton, a two-time Grand Slam semi-finalist, swept out Jakub Mensík in straight sets 6-3 6-1 in 72 minutes and is yet to drop a set in this tournament.

Image: Ben Shelton is the defending Canadian Open champion (Christinne Muschi/The Canadian Press via AP)

Should Jodar and Shelton meet in Thursday's final, a win for Jodar would also see him move into the top 10 and make history.

"I played a very high level against a tough player like Arthur," said Jodar after beating Filis.

"I had to give my best to win this match. It worked perfectly, staying calm in those important moments of the match, those pressure moments."

Image: Rafael Jodar (left) reached the quarter-finals at the French Open earlier this year (Christinne Muschi/The Canadian Press via AP)

Rybakina battles back to beat Osaka

Elena Rybakina rallied back after losing the opening set to defeat 11th-seed Naomi Osaka 4-6 7-6 (7-5) 6-4 and advance to the semi-finals of the WTA Canadian Open in Toronto.

Osaka came flying out of the blocks by breaking in the opening game which was enough to win the first set, before both players twice exchanged breaks in the second which Rybakina won on a tie-break.

The Kazakh made the decisive break in the seventh game of the last set and went on to win arguably the match of the tournament.

Image: Elena Rybakina would be just four ranking points behind Aryna Sabalenka if she wins the Montreal title (Julian Avram/Icon Sportswire/AP)

"Super happy. It was a very difficult match. In the first set [I made] a few mistakes, a poor start," said Rybakina, who could overtake Aryna Sabalenka as world No 1 later this month.

"It was a really tough one but I'm glad I could turn it around, I don't yet know how, but I think my serve helped me a little bit."

Rybakina will play Coco Gauff in the semi-finals after the American received a walkover in her quarter-final when her opponent Belinda Bencic withdrew due to a hip injury.

The other semi-final sees Iga Swiatek take on Elina Svitolina for a place in Thursday's final.

Sports.title: Today on Sky Sports Racing: Ffos Las hosts six-race card
Sports.content:
Don't miss a moment from Ffos Las on Wednesday, with all six races live from 3.37pm on Sky Sports Racing.

4.37 Ffos Las - Narrjoo headlines following promising debut

Narrjoo headlines a field of seven in the Meyer Timber EBF Maiden Stakes.

Simon and Ed Crisford's representative finished second to exciting Godolphin newcomer Jassas when impressing on debut at Doncaster last month and will be tough to beat if he can run to the same standard. This 200,000gns son of Ten Sovereigns has future entries in the Champagne Stakes and Goffs Million, which indicate how highly he is thought of at Gainsborough Stables.

Drum Bay and Isabella de Vega both similarly caught the eye on their respective debuts, and should provide a good level of opposition to Narrjoo for Ralph Beckett and Ed Walker respectively.

The most intriguing newcomer comes in the form of the 200,000gns two-year-old Mehmas colt Engraved, who could run well first time up for the James Fanshawe team.

3.37 Ffos Las - No Half Measures' half-sister clashes with Eskimo Pie

Eskimo Pie seeks her first success in the Faucets The Bathroom Specialists Maiden Fillies' Stakes but will have to get past No Half Measures' half-sister Mystic Veil, who makes her debut.

Eskimo Pie finished a good seventh in the 2025 Queen Mary Stakes before running lame on her final start at two in the Princess Margaret. Her first start at three was promising, but she subsequently underperformed in her next two tries. She was bumped when looking to challenge at Newmarket the last day and very much sets the standard at her peak for the Jane Chapple-Hyam team.

The Ed Walker-trained Mollstar showed a respectable level of form on her third run before being found reportedly lame after her last start in December. Returning from a break here, this filly is an interesting contender under Ashley Lewis.

Mystic Veil is a half-sister to July Cup winner No Half Measures and is trained by Archie Watson - a handler renowned for his success with two-year-olds. She could very well succeed on her first outing and a market watch is essential in the build-up.

Dixie Blue - a daughter of Starspangledbanner - also makes her first start, while Livvy's Edge completes the quintet.

6.10 Ffos Las - Belle Of Kt bids for another success

Belle Of Kt bids for a hat-trick in the Dress For The Occasions Handicap, wish closes the card at the Welsh track.

The admirably consistent mare has found some improvement of late, putting a couple of wins together within the space of eight days. She did not seem to have loads in hand last time out when scoring by a nose, but should put up a bold effort when attempting a hat-trick, with Millie Wonnacott's 5lb claim potentially crucial.

A Daughters Love should prove tough to beat following a facile 10-length victory when bouncing back to form down in grade last time out. She clearly enjoys this course and distance but has been raised 6lb for that victory.

Noble Grace also won over course and distance just two weeks ago, yet in contrasting fashion, battling well in a terrific finish.

Sports.title: 'Everyone can have an opinion' - F1 president responds to regulations criticism
Sports.content:
Formula 1 president Stefano Domenicali says drivers "can have their opinion" and are not being stopped from criticising the sport's power unit regulations.

The 2026 technical regulations have divided opinion with Max Verstappen among those to voice his concerns about the rules which have led to a different style of driving and racing.

Verstappen has previously described the yoyo style of racing - which sees passes then re-passes - as "anti-racing" and joked at last month's Belgian Grand Prix that someone would "probably shoot me outside the door" if he criticised the rules.

The Red Bull driver clarified a week later in Hungary: "I've spoken my mind about these regulations already a long time, and in the beginning, most people were saying, 'ah, he's complaining; he should shut up'.

"But I have to say that the last few races, more and more people are seeing the same thing that I could see coming already a long time, and it's not about me not liking not winning anymore.

"It's just because I care about the product, and because I've said it many times, and at one point that's also enough, right? But of course, when people keep asking you, then yeah, maybe it's not appreciated always, but I'm just speaking. I'm just speaking my mind because you see certain things coming, and then sometimes people say, 'yeah, but this was a great race'.

"I say, 'yeah, but it's not really realistic the way we are racing'. And then you arrive to some tracks, and yeah, you're driving on not a lot of horsepower for F1 standards, and it's a little bit painful, which I could see coming already for years. It's then, of course, not the most exciting. But at one point, I'm also a little bit just fed up with repeating myself because it's already hard enough just having to drive it."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton went wheel to wheel in a feisty scrap at the Austrian GP

Domenicali says he would prefer to discuss things behind closed doors to find solutions but respects all the drivers' opinions.

"You know me, we are not here to put tape on the mouth of anyone. The beauty of our sport is that everyone can have an opinion, but the opinion is an opinion," he said.

"There is someone who has the duty to have a line. There are certain drivers that prefer, of course, certain things. That in the process we have highlighted the need to be constructive in that respect."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Verstappen shocked Hamilton with a stunning overtake at the Hungarian Grand Prix

Domenicali: F1 is bigger than any driver

In March, Verstappen stated he was considering his future in the sport if the regulations did not change for next year, such was his dissatisfactions with the new power unit rules which have more electrical power compared to previous seasons.

The current split is nearly 50-50 between internal combustion and electrical power but the FIA announced in May it had agreed with the teams to change this to 58-42 for 2027 and 60-40 for 2028.

Since then, Verstappen has not suggested he will walk away from F1, although questions remain over whether he will drive for Red Bull or another team.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Craig Slater assesses what Verstappen's next move could be and whether the Red Bull driver may head to McLaren or Mercedes

Domenicali said: "Max is an incredible driver. I've stated so many times that maybe I'm getting older to repeat that!

"Max is in a situation where if he loves Formula 1. We discuss together the regulations for the future. I have an incredible relationship with him.

"F1 is big enough for him to be part of us, but of course he will decide his future, the way that he prefers to do. The sport will look ahead but my opinion is that Max will stay with us, and I really hope so, and that's what I'm stating. The sport is big, much bigger than anyone else, all of us."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hamilton and Charles Leclerc went head-to-head in their Ferrari's at the Chinese GP

Every F1 event this season has been sold out with record crowd attendances in Australia (484,000), Canada (360,000), Austria (320,000), Silverstone (564,000), Belgium (400,000) and Hungary (310,000).

Domenicali pointed to the continued growth of F1 and a conversation he had with filmmaker and creator of Star Wars, George Lucas, which shows the majority of fans are "not interested in how you drive the car" but instead whether there is overtaking or not.

"I had an incredibly interesting discussion with George Lucas on Saturday. He was in Hungary, and he was giving me an incredible view on how the new fans are watching Formula 1," he said.

"He gave us an incredible clearance to see how we can really simplify things because the new fans are not understanding the truth, what is behind the scenes.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch from onboard Alpine's Franco Colapinto as he pulls off an incredible double overtake on Pierre Gasly and Liam Lawson at the Belgian GP

"They are fascinated by the fact that there is a lot of action. There is definitely the need for those who are so focused on that to have the right information.

"But, for the vast majority of the people, trust me, they just want to see what is happening on the track, not interested in the angle of throttle or the percentage of brake pressure on how you can take and overtake a driver.

"For example, the incredible overtake of Max on Lewis at Turn 1 in Hungary, that was a piece of art, if I may say, that these people just want to see and just connect to the quality of the drivers."

Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 6: Chelsea
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 3rd (NB: this is not necessarily Billy Munday’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 10th

Prospects

After a season of struggle and regression, with two head coaches and two spells under a caretaker, there is cautious optimism that this campaign will bring something like stability. Much of that optimism centres around the appointment of Xabi Alonso, an elite manager with something to prove. There is also an expectation that the young players brought in as part of BlueCo’s £1.8bn splurge in recent years are beginning to come into their best years. There is no European football to complicate the schedule and a return to the Champions League by finishing in the top four or five would suffice for now. More importance will be placed on the domestic cups after a season without trophies.

Alonso’s squad is more rounded than what Enzo Maresca or Liam Rosenior had at their disposal. Maxence Lacroix and Morgan Rogers bring quality to positions where Chelsea were lacking it – at centre-back and out wide. Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson – the “uncs” as Tosin Adarabioyo has called them – will contribute as much off the pitch as on it. The signing of Marco Palestra, a specialist wing-back, suggests Alonso wants to be tactically flexible. He has used a back four and a back three in pre-season.

What about Cole Palmer? For so much of his time at Stamford Bridge, Chelsea’s form has been tied to his. When he has struggled to be 100% fit, the team have suffered too. After being omitted from England’s World Cup squad, Palmer had a seven-week break and sought advice from a specialist on the groin injury that hampered him last season. “I got bored after six weeks,” Palmer said after returning for pre-season. “I was sat in Marbella thinking: ‘I want to go back in.’” With the prospect of linking up with Rogers and João Pedro, who has also had a good rest, Palmer has plenty of reasons to be excited.

Off-field picture

July ended with Chelsea being fined £10m and receiving a suspended transfer ban over multiple violations of transfer rules under the ownership of Roman Abramovich. An appeal from the club saved them from a six-point deduction. Chelsea were deemed compliant with the Premier League’s profitability and sustainability rules for the three-year period ending in 2025 despite posting an English record £262.4m pre-tax loss for the 2024-25 season. They have not been cowed by failure to qualify for Europe and have spent over £300m on new signings. For the fourth year in a row, Chelsea look likely to start the season without a front-of-shirt sponsor.

Owner-fan relationship

Supporter protests against the ownership of Todd Boehly’s BlueCo have been a frequent sight on matchdays, including before May’s FA Cup final defeat by Manchester City. There have been reservations about the club’s youth-oriented transfer policy from the start and last season’s failings prompted the co-owner Behdad Eghbali to admit the need “to add more ready-made players” to the squad. Whether fans were expecting the arrivals of Welbeck and Henderson is another question. The introduction of a ticket ballot system for home games has also been unpopular with regular match-going supporters.

The manager

It was a bit of a coup for Chelsea to secure Alonso’s services this summer, especially given the Liverpool job was available. The Spaniard has a reputation to rebuild after his dream job at Real Madrid ended in the sack after six months. “I got a scar, now it is healed,” he said. Alonso’s record of developing young players, such as Florian Wirtz, at Bayer Leverkusen while simultaneously delivering silverware is a match made in heaven for the Chelsea hierarchy. One detail to note: Alonso has been appointed as manager, rather than head coach like his predecessors. He has also brought in Austin MacPhee, Aston Villa’s set-piece guru.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen Chelsea broke the British transfer record to pry Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa. Photograph: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty Images

Chelsea went one better than Manchester City’s £116m signing of Elliot Anderson by bringing in Rogers, who had been linked with Arsenal, for a new British record fee of £117m. Although he started England’s World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina on the right wing, Rogers has thrived for Aston Villa playing largely off the left and should slot in there nicely at Chelsea. The 24-year-old has proved himself in the Premier League and his best-buddy relationship with his former Manchester City youth teammate Palmer is a major plus. “I can see them linking really well,” Alonso said.

Stat attack

Has anyone checked Chelsea haven’t built a squad of Benjamin Buttons? The average age of their starting XI has decreased over the past three seasons when they were already the youngest team in Premier League history. You can see why they signed Henderson and Welbeck.

Set for a breakthrough

Robert Sánchez is still Chelsea’s No 1 but he may face serious competition this season from the 21-year-old Mike Penders. The goalkeeper, who was third-choice for Belgium at the World Cup, was signed from Genk in 2024 and spent last season on loan at Strasbourg in Ligue 1. The comparisons with Thibaut Courtois, who Chelsea signed from Genk at a similar age, are obvious. Like Courtois, Penders is 6ft 7in and therefore has a massive reach, but he also earns plaudits for his passing. Chances will come in cup competitions, but the clamour for Penders to be first choice might become hard to ignore.

World Cup impact

Enzo Fernández had a rollercoaster of a World Cup. Chelsea’s vice-captain popped up with crucial late goals for Argentina in the knockout stages, including a winning header against Egypt and the equaliser against England. But the abiding memory was his part in Argentina’s unsavoury approach in the final against Spain, where he received one yellow card for dissent and another for sending Pau Cubarsí flying. Real Madrid said in July they had “no intention” of pursuing a move that Fernández seemed to covet earlier this year when he said he would “love” to live in Madrid – comments that earned him a two-game ban under Rosenior. How about living in Manchester? City have been linked.

Sports.title: Saudi Pro League tries to move on from era of ageing megastar but big names still loom
Sports.content:
There’s no Mohamed Salah in the new Saudi Pro League season that kicks off on Thursday and while the age of the ageing megastar is ending, there is still the strong chance that the next few months will be dominated by Cristiano Ronaldo. The 41-year-old is 24 shy of 1,000 career goals and with the five-time Ballon d’Or winner having scored 102 in 107 league games for Al-Nassr so far, the milestone could – should – be reached this season.

Huge as that will be, just how it fits into the plans of the league is unclear. This is the fourth season since the spending started with $957m (£710m) splashed out in that summer of 2023. It delivered thousands of articles, dozens of international broadcasting deals and untold numbers of people worldwide sporting the yellow CR7 Al-Nassr shirt. Now, though, the focus is on getting a little more value for money and lifting not just the clubs but the standard of Saudi Arabian football in general.

An early World Cup elimination provoked plenty of questions (even if later results showed that draws against Uruguay and an impressive Cape Verde plus a sole loss to champions Spain wasn’t quite as bad as it first looked) with the main one being whether the money spent on the local league had resulted in a better standard of local players. As yet, it does not seem to be the case.

The league does not yet supply talent to Europe, or anywhere else. Of the 26-man World Cup squad only the right-back Saud Abdulhamid of Lens plays overseas. The consensus is that this has to change, and is heightened by the worry that too many of those who stay home don’t get enough minutes. Locals are often squeezed out by foreign talents, especially when it comes to creative, goalscoring and goalkeeping positions. The big spending has undoubtedly improved the standard of teams in general – Saudi sides have had increased success in Asian club competitions – but the national team has yet to see the benefit.

So while many expected Salah to choose the Red Sea over the Black Sea port of Trabzonspor, the determination to get the Egyptian seemed to have lessened over the past few months (and that’s assuming that Salah ever considered Saudi Arabia as his first choice). The biggest name in the Arab footballing world would have been quite a draw even if the 34-year-old no longer fits the preferred model, which is trying to sign younger players who have a resale value when they return to Europe.

It remains to be seen if that is the case for Crysencio Summerville, the biggest signing of the summer so far, who joined Al-Hilal for around €80m (£68m). If all goes well, the 24-year old Dutch winger can spend some time in Riyadh and, one day, head back to Europe for another hefty fee. There have been the usual criticisms of Summerville choosing money over ambition but ambition is part of the Hilal DNA. With 19 league titles and four Asian championships, coming second again will not be acceptable even if the team was undefeated through the whole campaign. The Blues, sold by the Public Investment Fund in April, still have Karim Benzema, Rúben Neves, Theo Hernández, Yassine Bounou, Kalidou Koulibaly and more so the pressure is on coach Simone Inzaghi to retake the title from the yellow half of Riyadh.

View image in fullscreen Lens’ Saud Abdulhamid is the only player from Saudi Arabia to play overseas. Photograph: Icon Sport/Alamy

Ronaldo lifted that trophy in May for Al-Nassr, a triumph soon followed by the exit of Jorge Jesus to take over Portugal. He has been replaced by Ange Postecoglou. The former Tottenham Hotspur manager has Sadio Mané, Kingsley Coman and João Félix at his disposal, but the club have financial issues which have meant that, as yet, there have not been many incomings. A first Asian Champions League title would go down well.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

That crown belongs to Al-Ahli, who after winning their second successive continental title in April were ready to focus on domestic matters this season and a second SPL title since 1984. It was all looking good but then, just a few days before the start, head coach Matthias Jaissle left for Newcastle. The Greens and the Magpies may share the same PIF owners but this was not a decision that went down well in Jeddah. The appointment of Arne Slot’s former assistant Marino Pusic is not seen as especially exciting. Jaissle’s departure also came as a shock to Jeddah rivals Al-Ittihad, who struggled last season. Just a day or so before Jaissle’s departure, the Tigers followed their rivals in hiring a 38-year-old German, whose career as a defender had also been cut short by injury and had experience at RB Salzburg. Jens Wissing has a big job ahead.

And Al-Qadsiah are the last of the contenders. If Brendan Rodgers can improve on last season’s fourth and also win a first trophy since 1984, that will be enough for the Aramco-backed club. There is now a genuine “big five” which provides challenges for the others but perhaps they can progress by giving more minutes and opportunities to local players which would, in the long-run, be better for the league than signing Salah and other players in their mid-30s.

Sports.title: Barcelona make improved £51m bid for Rodri as Manchester City target Fernández
Sports.content:
Barcelona have made an improved bid to Manchester City of around €60m (£51m) for Rodri.

This follows Barça’s initial offer of €45m that was rejected out of hand by City. The Spanish club’s new offer – which may include add-ons – is close to City’s valuation for the 30-year-old who captained Spain to the World Cup and won the Ballon d’Or in 2024.



As the midfielder has declared a preference for Barcelona it seems it is inevitable he will leave. In preparation City are targeting Chelsea’s Enzo Fernández as a potential signing though the west London club’s valuation of around £120m may be too high.

Chelsea are understood to be intent on that price for the attacking midfielder so any transfer may include add-ons. Enzo Maresca is keen on Fernández after working with him for a season-and-a-half at Chelsea before his tenure ended in January.

The 25-year-old was a key member of Maresca’s team that finished fourth and won the Europa Conference in 2024-25 and the Fifa Club World Cup last summer.

If City were to sign Fernández, a World Cup winner with Argentina in 2022, another midfielder could be offloaded, with Tijjani Reijnders a possible candidate to depart.

As Rodri is intent on a move to Barcelona the arrival of Fernández, Chelsea’s captain, would add seniority and leadership to Maresca’s squad and a player whose combative style would offer an edge to City’s play.

City have so far recruited Elliott Anderson for £116m from Nottingham Forest and are close to the signing of Ayyoub Bouaddi for around £85m from Lille.

Chelsea are thought to have enquired about Bournemouth’s Alex Scott as a replacement for Fernández should he leave.

On Wednesday City announced the signing of Gerónimo Rulli on a two-year deal following James Trafford’s move to Leeds. The Argentina goalkeeper was previously at the club in 2016-17.

The 35-year-old said: “My job now is to train hard, get to know the players and staff and do everything I can.”

Sports.title: ‘It is just smelling football’: Tielemans says adjusting to life at United has come naturally
Sports.content:
Youri Tielemans has stated that adjusting to Michael Carrick’s vision for Manchester United has been as easy as “smelling football” for the vastly experienced £35m midfield signing.

The 29-year-old, who joined from Aston Villa last month, made his debut for Anderlecht at the age of 16. He has been integrating with the United squad during the past 10 days of the club’s pre-season tour, making his first appearance in Saturday’s 1-1 draw with Paris Saint-Germain in Gothenburg.

Tielemans left Belgium for Monaco in 2017 and joined Leicester in 2019, before signing for Villa four years later and has 579 career appearances, so any demands from Carrick do not faze him.

Tielemans said: “He has got his structure. He wants to have the ball, he wants to press in certain ways, you know. It might be different than what you are used to, what I have been used to before, but it is logical things in my opinion. It is just smelling football, and that is what I have been doing from when I was young at Anderlecht.

“So for me, nothing changes, but it just needs to gel together. Then when you follow those principles, then you can add your offensive qualities, especially in the last third where everything is a bit more in freedom, without obviously overcommitting and keeping the defensive line in place, then I think we can do good things.”

Tielemans was limited to only 25 starts in the Premier League last season due to injury and also sustained a hamstring problem in the warm-up before Belgium’s World Cup quarter-final against Spain in July. Yet despite this and having already played for 13 years in midfield, Tielemans denied that Carrick will need to rest him on occasion.

He said: “Not really. The thing is, at the World Cup, I think we played 120 minutes against Senegal [before Spain], and from there we had less time in between games. So we played the US I think three or four days later [actually five days] and then three days later we played against Spain. In the warm-up, my body just switched off for some reason. Now, I do not think I am a player that I absolutely need a rest. Obviously, there are a lot of games and the manager needs to manage the team, but when I am good, I am good, you know.

“Unfortunately, my body is … when it does not go well, then I will know straight away and I will alert the manager, but it does not happen often.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

United previously showed interest in signing the Belgium captain, reportedly in 2019 and 2022. “There has been two times that I spoke with the club, but it did not achieve to anything, so I was just very calm about it. It was way after Anderlecht,” Tielemans said.

United, who triggered his release clause, did not face any competition to sign the player. “Not that I am aware of, no,” Tielemans said.

Sports.title: Football transfer rumours: Folarin Balogun to Tottenham? Gabriel Jesus to Napoli?
Sports.content:
Bradley Barcola is firmly in Liverpool’s sights as they look to rebuild their attack in the post-Mohamed Salah era. The two-time Champions League winner reportedly wants to leave Paris Saint-Germain, and Anfield is his preferred destination, though Arsenal have apparently been making eyes at the France international too. For their part PSG are thought to be closing on deals for Barcelona’s World Cup winner Ferran Torres and the Ajax winger Mika Godts, though the 21-year-old Belgium international had talked at the weekend of “putting an end” to rumours that he was refusing to play for Ajax in order to force a move.

England’s World Cup cult hero Djed Spence could soon be exhibiting his marauding runs and eye-catching slide tackles in Serie A. Inter are interested in a £25.6m move for the Tottenham full-back, who fancies a move to San Siro and might find himself struggling for regular first-team football in north London after Roberto De Zerbi’s busy summer in the market.

Napoli are stepping up their interest in Gabriel Jesus, who could be available for around €20m (£17m). With the Arsenal striker entering the final year of his contract at the Emirates and first-team opportunities with the English champions likely to be limited, Jesus could be amenable to a move. Arsenal meanwhile are keen on Jules Koundé, reports the Mirror, but an awful lot of ifs and ands are in play around the Barcelona and France full-back. For one Koundé is happy to stay at the Camp Nou, even if Barça might be prepared to cash in on a player with four years remaining on his contract, and the Spanish champions’ preferred replacement, Pedro Porro, has five years to go on his after recently signing a new deal with Tottenham.

As for Spurs, a rumoured target is controversy’s Folarin Balogun. L’Equipe says talks have been initiated with Monaco about a €60m (£51.2m) move for the USA and former Arsenal striker, who impressed at the World Cup. Another Monaco player attracting Premier League interest is the winger Igor Paixao, at whom Leeds continue to make eyes. The Ligue 1 club’s manager, Bruno Genesio, is eager to keep the Brazilian though.

Mykhailo Mudryk could be sent to Coventry on his return from drug-ban limbo. Chelsea are open to loan offers for the Ukrainian winger and Frank Lampard’s newly promoted side have jostled their way to the front of the queue, according to football.london.

Everton are weighing up their interest in three full-backs – Celtic’s Alastair Johnson, West Ham’s Aaron Wan-Bissaka and the English right-back Brooke Norton-Cuffy, who has been at Genoa since 2024. David Moyes will also be cheered by news that Iliman Ndiaye has reportedly turned down a move to the Saudi Pro League’s Al-Hilal. Fulham meanwhile like the look of the 20-year-old Barcelona defender Hector Fort, who spent last season on loan at Elche and does not appear to have a future at the Camp Nou.

And Wednesday’s Manchester United rumour has the Red Devils in for the Club Brugge left-back Joaquin Seys. The 21-year-old Belgium international would set them back around £30m.

Sports.title: League One 2026-27 preview: the contenders, hopefuls and strugglers
Sports.content:
Contenders

How did it come to this, that a club crowned Premier League champions a decade ago are down in the third tier? Chronic mismanagement across the board has been Leicester’s problem for too long and they need to reset under Russell Martin. Many of the top earners have been shipped out and not much brought in, but there remains enough quality to challenge at this level. Martin has at his disposal plenty of young talents who could finally be given their chance thanks to circumstance and who will be ably supported by Harry Souttar and Stephy Mavididi.

It is all change at Stockport after Jimmy McNulty replaced the long‑serving Dave Challinor following defeat in the playoff final. A strategy of signing youngsters has been implemented under a coach known for improving players. Stockport are, however, a slick operation and know the value of experience, with Ben Osborn, returning permanently after impressing on loan last season, and Eoghan O’Connell brought in on free transfers.

New ownership and a squad overhaul make it difficult to assess Sheffield Wednesday but signing Louie Barry is a sign of intent. Whether they can get the best out of the forward will go a long way to determining where they finish.

Jack Wilshere has had time to settle at Luton and understands the relentlessness needed at this level. The additions of Kasey Palmer permanently and Callum Marshall will add plenty of thrust. Things seem more settled around Reading, who have brought in the former Accrington manager John Coleman as Leam Richardson’s assistant, which could prove a shrewd move.

View image in fullscreen Jack Wilshere will be aiming to kick on now he has settled at Luton. Photograph: Marc Atkins/Getty Images

After missing out in the playoff semis, Bradford have been tweaking the squad as they try to improve. Callum Connolly’s arrival is smart, while Adam Phillips will add plenty in central midfield. Plymouth have come down and lost the striker Lorent Tolaj to Bristol City, but Tom Cleverley will feel he has enough in the ranks, with Will Evans tasked with being the new goal threat.

Hopefuls

Martin Drury is in his first senior managerial role at Huddersfield but has surrounded himself with knowhow, such as Alan Knill. Procuring Matty Young on loan from Sunderland and signing Ashley Fletcher provides an upgrade at each end of the pitch. MK Dons moved quickly to build on promotion, bringing in players who have proved themselves at this level; Ryan Wintle, Cohen Bramall, Dan Barlaser, Sam Silvera and Sam Nombe have not joined just to make up the numbers.

Promotion pushes at Wigan and Blackpool appear unlikely, with neither’s transfer business suggesting a surge up the table. The Latics have focused on younger players, while the Tangerines have barely made a splash. Daniel Stendel is back at Barnsley, tasked with getting the most out of a young squad, with star turns such as Reyes Cleary. Everyone is excited to learn about Aaron Ramsey as a full-time manager at Oxford, wh could go either way at a club in­ flux. Frankie Kent injuring his ACL less than a month after signing was a blow, magnified because he was one of only two incomings the club managed to get over the line before the EFL imposed a transfer embargo, and fans do not expect a quick return upwards on account of a lack of depth in the squad.

There is no desire for another relegation battle at Leyton Orient. Fin Stevens, Joseph Olowu and Isaac Hayden will inject quality and defensive steel. Dom Ballard’s departure takes away a lot of goals but the club were quick to reinvest in the club-record signing Jaze Kabia from Grimsby. With Michael Duff settled in the Wycombe hotseat, there is a prospect something can be built on the foundations of Steve Cook, a free transfer at the back. The losses of Charlie Goode and Harvey White are a blow to Stevenage, but they have a smart coach in Alex Revell, who will relish the challenge. With Mikel Arteta the only manager in English professional football who has been in his role longer than Nigel Clough, Mansfield will be hoping longevity is the secret ingredient. Either that or acquiring David McGoldrick and Michael Smith to create a strike partnership with a combined age of 72.

View image in fullscreen Nigel Clough’s new strike pairing at Mansfield, David McGoldrick and Michael Smith, have a combined age of 72. Photograph: David Rogers/Getty Images

Peterborough are always hard to predict because they have a lot of young talent with great potential but that does not always translate to success at this level. Doncaster will be aiming to build on a comfortable mid-table finish upon their return to the third tier, with the goalkeeper Tommy Simkin an impressive loan signing from Stoke.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Strugglers

Notts County’s summer transfer business is aligned with their statistics-based recruitment model but signing two players who were relegated from League Two, among others, suggests the playoff winners are in for a battle, especially after selling the star striker Alassana Jatta. The League Two champions Bromley are on a meteoric rise and find themselves mixing with some much bigger clubs, without the resources to match. After two consecutive seasons finishing one place above the dropzone, Burton know their reality. Corey Addai is an upgrade in goal but doubts linger if Matthew Dennis can replace Jake Beesley up front.

Cambridge came up automatically and have signed players with knowhow in this league to complement the talented Ben Knight. AFC Wimbledon would be happy with survival at this stage after a quiet summer, but are safe in the knowledge that Jayden Stockley will bring goals.

Ones to watch

James Bailey, Stockport, 18 A free transfer after spending his formative years at Manchester United, the left-footed teenager is an old-school midfielder, wanting to win the ball but with the ability to play. When he signed, he caused much mirth because his grizzled looks give the impression of a man twice his age.

Will Grainger, Sheffield Wednesday, 17 Attracted Premier League interest but the Owls fan, who joined the club aged eight, did not contemplate leaving and signed a three-year deal. Very good technically, the Wales youth international is a clever No 10 with an eye for a pass and goal.

Vimal Yoganathan, Barnsley, 20 Good with both feet, the central midfielder became a regular last season and will be hoping to push on. A clever player who also possesses speed and determination, the 20-year-old has received international recognition with Wales.

Sports.title: Infantino’s opponents developing new framework for running world football
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino’s opponents are working together to produce a new framework for running world football to replace what they regard as a system of patronage that Fifa has adopted since he replaced Sepp Blatter as president 10 years ago.

Repeated calls from Uefa, Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation for an independent review of Fifa’s governance have been ignored by Infantino since his plan to sell off 21% of the World Cup was made public a fortnight ago, and the rebels are now understood to have taken matters into their own hands.

A source with knowledge of the discussions told the Guardian that the three confederations are working on producing a policy document to demonstrate how the world governing body could evolve in the future.

Those involved have been empowered to ask existential questions such as what Fifa’s precise role should be, how it should be structured and what governance model should be adopted. Financial distribution among member associations is also a key consideration, particularly with an eye on how best to deploy funds from Fifa’s estimated $5bn (£3.7bn) reserves.

If Infantino refuses to engage then the new framework is likely to be adopted by a challenger at the presidential election next year, or could even serve as a template for a breakaway organisation.

After releasing a joint statement on Monday, which called for “leadership that serves football, not seeks to command it”, Uefa, Concacaf and the AFC let it be known that they have begun preliminary discussions about organising new competitions if the standoff with Fifa’s leadership persists.

View image in fullscreen Uefa officials are meeting in Salzburg where the Super Cup takes place on Wednesday between Paris Saint-Germain and Aston Villa. Photograph: Gintare Karpaviciute/Reuters

At present the Under-20 Women’s World Cup next month could take place without European teams, as Uefa is maintaining that its members will boycott the tournament, unless Fifa moves quickly to set up an independent review of the World Cup sell‑off debacle and provide legally binding assurances that such a move will not be repeated.

The Concacaf president, Victor Montagliani, is seen as the most likely presidential challenger to Infantino at this stage – although, as he told the Guardian in June, his current focus is on being reelected as president of the North and Central American confederation next year.

It seemed significant, however, that the joint statement released on Monday contained strong echoes of a speech given by Montagliani at the Fifa congress this year in Vancouver, where he said: “Let me be frank, leadership is not about power.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Senior figures from European football are gathering in person for the first time since the Fifa Forward Enterprise scandal broke, with a number of meetings expected in Salzburg – where the Uefa Super Cup final will be held on Wednesday – over the next two days.

The Uefa president, Aleksander Ceferin, will hold talks with Nasser al-Khelaifi, the chair of European Football Clubs, aimed at reinforcing the continent’s unity in demanding a change at the top of Fifa.

Uefa continues to hold firm in its pledge to boycott Fifa competitions, having not received its desired assurances that there will be no recurrence of the issues that caused the current crisis.

Sports.title: Which footballer has played for the most clubs in their career? | The Knowledge
Sports.content:
“Which footballer has played for the most clubs?” asks Paul Gage.

Surprisingly, throughout the more than two decades of the Knowledge, this question has not been answered before. But, fear not, it will be now.

Before we consult the Guinness World Records book, we should doff our cap to somebody who, though well short of the world record, has just moved to their 19th club. “At the age of 45,” writes Mike Kilner, “Derek Asamoah – best known for scoring at Anfield for Carlisle in the Carabao Cup – will be looking to bang them this weekend for his 19th different club, Whitstable Town.”

There is an official answer and an unofficial one. Let’s start with the official. According to Guinness WR HQ, the Uruguayan striker Sebastián Abreu played for the most professional clubs as he competed for 31 different sides across his 26-year career. Abreu, who is the manager of Tijuana, started his playing career in 1995 and retired in 2021. However, unofficially, there is a player who has competed for 20 (!) more clubs than Abreu – Jefferson Louis recorded 51 clubs in a 28-year career.

The Naming XI

“The Wrexham defender Max Cleworth has the letters of ‘Wrexham’ within his name,” notes Mark Lumby. “Have any other players had their club within their own name?”

We had dozens of answers to this, so thank you to one and all. We’ve whittled them down into a star-studded XI as follows. But first, some reasonably arbitrary rules:

1. Prefixes and suffixes like United, City, FC, AC aren’t included.

2. Letters in a player’s name can’t be used twice – in other words, Dani Alves (Sevilla) doesn’t qualify because his name only has one of the two Ls in Sevilla.

Manuela Zinsberger (Arsenal)

Lauren Bisan (Arsenal)

Lucas Radebe (Leeds)

Paolo Maldini (Milan)

Ashley Cole (Chelsea)

Trevor Steven (Everton)

Michael Essien (Chelsea)

Neymar da Silva Santos Júnior (Santos)

Alan Sunderland (Arsenal)

Frank Stapleton (Arsenal)

Victor Anichebe (Everton)

Now this one is a bit more obscure in terms of football knowledge, but the anagram element is easier to spot. David Ekstrand emails: “With regard to Mark Lumby’s question, Ian Sirelius played 152 games for Swedish club Sirius, starting in the third tier and ending in the top flight.”

Dave Mellinger says answers are easier to find in America: “This challenge is probably easier in the States, where teams aren’t necessarily named after their cities, than in Britain. My local NWSL team is the [Portland] Thorns, for which defender Cheyenne Shorts qualifies. An even shorter team name is Bay (FC), for which Dorian Bailey, Brooklyn Courtnall, and Abby Dahlkemper qualify. In fact, Dorian Bailey’s last name works by itself, as does Dahlkemper’s first name.”

View image in fullscreen Abby Dahlkemper celebrates Women’s World Cup glory with the USA in 2019 – in 2024 she moved to a club whose name can be made from the letters in her first name. Photograph: NurPhoto/Getty Images

“By no means exhaustive and I had to take a bit of leeway with some middle names,” Russell Yong emails. “But here are a few examples …”

Arsenal: Alan Sunderland, Tony Alexander Adams

Chelsea: Michael Essien; Ruben Ira Loftus-Cheek

Celtic: Carlton Michael Cole

Leeds: Eddie Lewis

Leicester: Kasper Peter Schmeichel

West Ham: Matthew Upson

Stuart Basson has taken the next step with his answer. He writes: “Not only did the following players have their club’s letters in their name, their surname was their club’s name!”

Ben Barnett (Barnet) 1993-94

Lewis Bradford (Bradford City) 1940s

Arthur Blackburn (Blackburn Rovers) 1899

Ronnie Bolton (Bolton Wanderers) 1898

Frank Burton (Burton Swifts) 1898

Jimmy Shields (South Shields) 1961

The biggest leap in levels between games, pt II

In last week’s Knowledge, we looked at players who jumped several levels from one professional game to the next. “Kevin Keegan deserves a mention,” writes John Neal. “He played for Scunthorpe v Brentford in the old Fourth Division (they finished 17th) before making his debut for Liverpool against Nottingham Forest in the First Division (and scoring 12 minutes into the game). Liverpool finished third that season, one point behind Derby and level on points with Manchester City and Leeds.”

View image in fullscreen Kevin Keegan goes airborne for Liverpool against Zurich in the 1976-77 European Cup semi-final, second leg. Six years earlier he made the leap from fourth tier to first when he left Scunthorpe. Photograph: PA Archive/PA Images

Alan Burgess suggests Chris Smalling and Maximilian Kilman, who both took a shortcut from non-league to Premier League: Maidstone to Fulham in Smalling’s case, Maidenhead to Wolves in Kilman’s. Alan Shoulder jumped from Blyth Spartans (Northern League) to Newcastle (the old Division Two) in 1978; thanks to Richard Slassor for that one. And, finally, Liverpool legend Roger Hunt joined them straight from Stockton Heath (which later became Warrington Town) in 1958.

“Mikel Arteta (one title) is the only manager with title-winning experience (in England) heading into the new season. Is this the only time since 1889-90 that there is only a single title among the managers at the start of the season?” asks Jeremy Finch.

This question has quickly been debunked by Paul Waite. He says: “Everton manager David Moyes took the Division Two (third tier) title with Preston in 1999-2000 and Manchester City head honcho Enzo Maresca won the Championship with Leicester in 2023-24.”

But if Jeremy means the Premier League title specifically, then this season Arteta is the only manager to have won it from the dugout. There has been another occasion where this has happened, in the 1891-92 season with the then Everton manager, Dick Molyneux, having the only top-flight title-winning experience. But if anyone can find another season that you think we may have missed, email the usual place.

Knowledge archive

“After listening to Arsenal fans moaning following their 3-0 defeat by Chelsea, I wondered: has a manager ever been sacked because of poor pre-season results?” asked Paul Cartwright in 2017.

We have previously looked at managers who were sacked during the summer break, though not specifically at those who lost their job because of pre-season results. So here’s Oliver Robinson, waiting to tell us a story. “I’ll take you down to Hampshire,” says Oliver, “where, in 2015, Bashley sacked their manager – the ex-Chelsea, Millwall and Dallas Sidekicks defender David Stride – after five and a half weeks. The Bash said that it was because of ‘a run of poor pre-season results and lack of player signings’ although the run wasn’t that bad: four games, no goals, eight conceded.”

There was a variation on this theme during the USSR’s preparation for the 1986 World Cup. “The manager, Eduard Malofeyev, was sacked a month before the start of the competition, specifically due to ‘poor results in friendlies’,” says Marat Airapetian. “The replacement was the great Valeriy Lobanovskyi, which was only natural, considering that out of 22 players in the squad, 12 represented his club, Dynamo Kyiv.”

View image in fullscreen A statue commemorating Valeriy Lobanovskyi in Kyiv. He made an eye-popping impact for the Soviet Union when he took over just before the 1986 World Cup. Photograph: Anastasia Vlasova/The Guardian

In that case, the end justified the means. The USSR were one of the teams of the tournament, even though they went out in the last 16. They thrashed Hungary 6-0 and scored umpteen long-range screamers before losing 4-3 to Belgium in a thriller.

Finally, it’s our old friend Jørn Andersen, who was included in the previous link about managers who were sacked during the summer. It seems there were a few reasons he got the boot, one of them being that old devil called results.

“If we define pre-season as including pre-league season, then he definitely qualifies,” says Julian Unkel. “He took over Mainz from Jürgen Klopp before the 2008-09 season and achieved promotion to the Bundesliga. However, during the 2009-10 pre-season, differences arose between Andersen and the club about his methods (for example, he would not allow his players to hang family pictures in the dressing room). After several underwhelming pre-season results, Mainz were also eliminated in the first round of the German Cup by fourth-tier team Lübeck. Andersen was sacked on 3 August 2009, four days before the first league game, and replaced by Thomas Tuchel.”

And in 2017 there was this.

Can you help?

“Gianluca Vialli was the first non-British manager to win the League Cup in 1998, while he was also player-manager. As far as I can tell, this would also make him the first player-manager to win the competition. Did someone else beat him to it?” asks Tom Stevenson.

“Birmingham’s August Priske scored the only goal at Swansea in the League Cup on 8 August. Can you think of any other examples of matching name of scorers and months? Solly March in March?” wonders Paul Tiffen.

“Celtic and Rangers have played each other a whopping 452 times. Is there a rivalry in world football that can top that? Alec Smith played in 87 Old Firm games for Rangers between 1894 and 1913. Has any player faced a rival on more occasions?” questions Brian Arthur.

“Why are some football transfer fees undisclosed? Doesn’t seem to be particular clubs, just random. Who benefits from keeping the fee private?” asks Rob.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace youngster has loan terminated after a month to join another EFL club in same division
Sports.content:
All recommendations within this article are informed by expert editorial opinion. If you click on a link in this story we will earn affiliate revenue.

Crystal Palace youngster has loan terminated after a month to join another EFL club in same division

Young Crystal Palace midfielder Hindolo Mustapha has left Wigan Athletic after barely a month on loan with the club.

The 20-year-old joined Wigan on a season-long loan in early July, but the deal has been terminated before the start of the new League One campaign.

2 Mustapha was named Crystal Palace Under-21s Player of the Season for his performances in Premier League 2 in 2024/25 Credit: Getty

But Mustapha will still begin the season in the third tier having made another loan move, this time to newly promoted Notts County.

Announcing Mustapha's departure on their website, Wigan explained: "After a period of adapting to his surroundings, it was felt that a change would be beneficial for all parties. Hindolo now returns to Selhurst Park to continue the next stage of his development."

The Sierra Leone international featured for Wigan in pre-season but was not included in the squad for their first competitive game of the campaign, Saturday's Carabao Cup first-round defeat on penalties to Barnsley.

Having joined Palace's youth set-up at U9 level, Mustapha went on to sign his first professional contract at Selhurst Park in January 2024.

He has yet to break into the Eagles' first team but did make two appearances for their U21 side in the 2024/25 EFL Trophy, scoring once.

And unfortunately for Mustapha, this isn't his first loan spell that hasn't worked out.

Loaned out to German second-tier outfit Nurnberg for the first half of last term, he returned to Palace in January without having played a single minute.

During that stint, Nurnberg boss Miroslav Klose appeared to question Mustapha's attitude.

"He has something that I like," Klose said. "That’s why I will support him – but only up to a certain point. But we brought him in because he has to perform here.

"It's not like in London, where he can stroll through the city and go shopping," he said. "Perhaps it's a bit different in Nuremberg. We need time to settle in a bit, but we won't be able to manage without him. He needs to know where our limits are, where everything starts with discipline."

Mustapha subsequently spent the second half of the 2025/26 campaign with Championship West Brom, though he only featured twice for the Baggies.

2 Mustapha made a sole Championship appearance for West Brom Credit: Getty

He'll be hoping to be more involved for Martin Paterson's Notts County, who host Leicester in their League One opener this Saturday.

Mustapha is one of three players Palace have loaned out so far this summer.

Goalkeeper Owen Goodman and left-back Rio Cardines have joined Dundee and Bristol City respectively, both on season-long loans.

Palace begin the new Premier League campaign away to Everton next Saturday.

It's the start of a new era for the Eagles, now managed by Pierre Sage following the departure of FA Cup and Conference League-winning boss Oliver Glasner, who has since taken over at Nottingham Forest.

Sports.title: Jamie O’Hara accuses Gabby Agbonlahor of ‘bottling it’ for Brennan Johnson apology
Sports.content:
Gabby Agbonlahor has apologised to Brennan Johnson for disparaging comments about his swap deal and called on Jamie O'Hara to do the same.

Everton and Crystal Palace completed a straight swap with Dwight McNeil moving to Selhurst Park, while Johnson headed to the Hill Dickinson.

3 Everton can call upon Brennan Johnson after the Wales international sealed his switch from Crystal Palace Credit: Everton FC

It seemed a surprising transfer after the Eagles made Johnson their club-record £35million signing just six months ago; however, his brief stint in south London drew heavy criticism after he failed to score in 26 appearances.

On Tuesday, Agbonlahor questioned the deal on talkSPORT, pointing out that neither winger had scored a Premier League goal last term.

O'Hara replied: "It’s like, ‘We’ll give you crap, you give us crap back. Call it quits, no charge’."

A clip of their discussion quickly went viral, prompting Johnson to defend himself on social media. The Wales international commented under the post: 'Won more than both of these put together.'

Agbonlahor and O'Hara on Johnson Agbonlahor said: "When I saw it, I was like 'I get it'. Certain managers and certain players suit one another. Maybe David Moyes is looking at it and wants more pace in the side, wanting to use him in that way. "Also, with Dwight McNeil, there was talk he was leaving in January, and the new [Palace] manager has clearly seen enough of him already and wants to bring him in." O'Hara replied: "Brennan Johnson has been a myth for a few seasons. He didn’t do it at Spurs. In one of our seasons he got top scorer, but he hides in big games." Agbonlahor pointed out: "You look at both of them and their output last season - 16 Premier League appearances for Spurs, two goals, zero assists. Then at Palace, zero goals and one assist. "But then Dwight McNeil last season: 22 appearances in the Premier League, zero goals, one assist, so he’s not doing enough either." O'Hara replied: "It’s like ‘We’ll give you crap, you give us crap back. Call it quits, no charge’. "I like McNeil. If I were to pick which player would I rather have, I’d take Dwight McNeil. He’s going to work hard, with a lovely left foot. He gives you something. "Brennan Johnson is just so frustrating because he’s got all the attributes." He added: "Maybe it’s a confidence thing, maybe David Moyes might be the right manager for him. He’s got the right attributes, he showed it at Nottingham Forest."

Agbonlahor backtracks on air

On Wednesday morning, Agbonlahor issued an apology live on air: "What did I do wrong? It was Jamie who said it. I want to say sorry to Brennan Johnson, I should not have laughed.

"When someone laughs, it’s natural to start laughing. However, I think Jamie O’Hara was out of order and I think he needs to apologise on the 4pm Drive show.

"I think he has to, he can’t say ‘crap for crap.'"

This prompted O'Hara to take to X to clarify his stance: "This the prob when you only listen to a clip and not full story.

"We were talking about Brennan and McNeil stats from last season which were CRAP not that they were bad players.

"I’m a fan of McNeill and also said Brennan has all the attributes but he would admit his season was crap."

3 O'Hara hit back at comments claiming Johnson did not hear the full context Credit: talkSPORT

Additionally, he followed up his original post, saying: "Gabby bottling it as usual it’s not that deep guys stats are stats and they ain’t great viewing I hope Brennan gets 20 goals this season."

'Stats are stats'

Johnson publicly called out the punditry duo, pointing out that his list of career honours is far greater than O'Hara and Agbonlahor's combined.

The new Everton forward has won two major European trophies, including the Conference League with Palace last season.

Additionally, Johnson wrote his name into Tottenham history by scoring the winning goal in the Europa League final against Manchester United in 2025.

Like O'Hara, Johnson spent time at Spurs, scoring 27 goals across three seasons in north London.

The 25-year-old finished as the club's top goalscorer in the 2024/25 campaign, accumulating 18 goals in all competitions.

3 talkSPORT's Gabby Agbonlahor is Aston Villa's record Premier League goalscorer Credit: Getty

Agbonlahor also added: “I'm not a petty guy, but if I wanted to respond to Brennan Johnson he said he didn't do it at Spurs. Then he said he got top goalscorer. Make your mind up, Jamie.

“But if I wanted to be petty, I would read out some stats, I'm going to be petty. Brennan Johnson, 140 Premier League appearances, 26 goals, 20 assists.

“He’s not really Brennan Ronaldo is he?”

By comparison, talkSPORT host O'Hara netted seven times across six seasons as a defender with the Lilywhites and won the League Cup in 2008.

Agbonlahor, meanwhile, enjoyed a long career at boyhood club Aston Villa, scoring 87 goals across 13 seasons in the Midlands.

However, as Johnson pointed out, the former striker finished his career without a single piece of silverware.

While the 25-year-old winger endured a difficult 2025/26 campaign, he will now aim to silence his critics as he embarks on a new chapter on Merseyside.

Sports.title: EFL club urged to make shock bid to sign Paul Pogba after career setback
Sports.content:
Carlton Cole has admitted he would bring the soon-to-be free agent Paul Pogba to West Ham United this summer.

Various reports have claimed that Pogba is set to leave AS Monaco via mutual agreement a little over a year after joining the club.

4 Pogba appears to be on his way out of Monaco Credit: Getty

The former Manchester United and Juventus midfielder, who won the 2018 World Cup with France, has played just 115 minutes for Monaco.

Pogba has dealt with fitness and injury issues following an 18-month doping ban, and is now set to be without a club.

It marks a sad chapter in the talented 33-year-old's career having been a star player in the Premier League and Serie A.

Reacting to the news on The Sports Bar, Jason Cundy asked former West Ham star Cole if he would bring him to the London Stadium.

Should West Ham sign Pogba?

"We know he was a fantastic talent," Cole said. "Whether he's fulfilled his talent or not... he's won the World Cup."

On Pogba's return to United in 2016, he added: "He went to Man United at a time when they were struggling and they all depended on him, because he was the marquee signing.

"It didn't quite work out... he did deliver at times, but it was sparse, underwhelming."

Cundy asked Cole if he would take him at West Ham: "You know what he's got under the bonnet, you know what he's capable of.

"£40k-a-week in the Championship, is that something that you think A, would appeal to West Ham and B, would appeal to him?"

"I don't know whether he wants to play in the Championship, for one, but he might be short of offers now... Yeah, I would take him," Cole said.

4 Cole would be willing give Pogba a chance of redemption at West Ham Credit: AFP

"I'd take a punt, but you'll have to sit down and have a conversation with him, and see where his head is at first, then you could probably go forward with that.

"There's another reason why you could sign him, to sell shirts. Kids love him!"

West Ham would make a real statement of intent if they were to sign Pogba as they bid to win promotion back to the Premier League.

They are one of the favourites to win the Championship and have a void to fill with the exit of Mateus Fernandes to Tottenham Hotspur.

Could Pogba retire after his Monaco exit?

Although Pogba is still in his 30's, European football journalist Andy Brassell has questioned if he should retire from professional football.

"Injured again this week," he explained. "This time in a training camp, ironically in England. They've been at St. George's Park this week, Monaco.

4 West Ham would make one of the signings of the summer if they brought in Pogba Credit: Getty

"Signed a year ago, cried tears of joy getting back in the game, but it's been an enormously frustrating experience for him. I'm led to believe he's been really useful in terms of the experience and the big brother role he's used in the dressing room.

"But ultimately, they want to see him on the pitch, and he's not been fit enough to play.

"Really, you just want him to be in a competition where he is going to be able to play, where he's just going to be able to enjoy himself for the last couple of years of his career, because the last year has been a pretty miserable experience."

When asked about what level he could play at, he added: "We don't know, because when did we last see him play? He's been out of the game for three years, basically.

"You can't count him as being a player, really, last season because he played just a handful of minutes for Monaco. He's clearly not up to Ligue 1 football physically, so I honestly don't know.

"MLS is quite physical - we know he's really into American culture but again, could he manage that? There's no evidence to suggest that he could. So, maybe we're looking at the Middle East, or maybe he just decides to call it quits."

4 How Pogba would look in a West Ham shirt

"It would be a shame," Brassell said. "But, there must be a point where you think, 'I can't do this anymore', in terms of the struggle. He's in a comfortable financial position with a young family, people love his company, he's a great person to be around.

"It just doesn't look like fun at the moment anymore. I know everyone wants to go out on their own terms, but very few footballers can."
