Sports.title: Memphis Depay declares war on Corinthians as they make him unemployed
Sports.content:
Memphis Depay declares war on Corinthians as they make him unemployed

Memphis Depay has slammed Corinthians for 'unacceptable' behaviour after they failed to renew his contract.

The Brazilian giants have chosen not to keep the former Manchester United forward at the club despite appearing to promise they would do so.

3 Depay is now a free agent, but he believes promises have been broken Credit: Getty

In a statement, Corinthians confirmed he was being released.

They stated that it was for financial reasons.

However, Depay has claimed that he had agreed a two-year extension verbally, only for it to be snatched away.

In a statement on X, he said: "Very disappointed to read that Corinthians decided not to honour our agreement in place to extend my contract for 2 more years.

"This renewal was explicitly agreed upon by the president as well as the sporting, legal and financial department.

"Some people decided however to breach this engagement... I didn't want this situation and always respected the club throughout the process, but now I am forced to react strongly in order to preserve my interests.

"In the upcoming days I will speak publicly but rest assured that I will not leave this unacceptable behaviour unsanctioned."

Messy situation

Depay's public response followed a statement from Corinthians in which they confirmed that Depay would be leaving the club.

They said: “Sport Club Corinthians Paulista has decided not to renew the contract of athlete Memphis Depay.

“This decision was taken solely and exclusively in consideration of the financial health of our institution, which demands rigorous balance and responsibility in the management of available resources.

“We would like to express our deep gratitude to player Memphis Depay and his entire team, who from the start of negotiations sought the best possible agreement.

“To the athlete in particular, the Club is eternally grateful for the dedication and the results achieved throughout his journey with us, which include 79 matches played, 20 goals scored and, above all, the conquest of three important titles: the Paulistao and the Copa do Brasil, in 2025; and the Supercopa Rei, in 2026.

3 Depay is the all-time top Dutch goalscorer and still has a few years left in his career Credit: Getty

“These achievements will certainly remain as a fundamental part of Corinthians’ history.

“We understand that the process extended beyond the traditional deadline, but this is mainly due to the fact that we are dealing with a differentiated athlete.

“The Board also recognises and values the tireless efforts of all the institution’s departments that worked to make the athlete’s stay feasible.

“However, after careful analysis, exclusively financial reasons and the commitment to responsible management of the Club prevailed.

“Given Corinthians’ current and future financial obligations, it became clear that taking on a new commitment of this magnitude would not be compatible, at this moment, with the financial balance we need to preserve to ensure the institution’s sustainability.

“We recognise that this was a difficult decision, but undoubtedly necessary for the future of Sport Club Corinthians Paulista.

“To clarify any doubts and discuss this matter in greater detail, the Club will organise a press conference in the coming days, during which president Osmar Stabile will be available to provide all necessary clarifications.

“We thank everyone for their understanding and will continue working so that Corinthians remains strong, solid, and victorious.”

Depay's time at Corinthians

The 32-year-old joined the Brazilian giants after being released by Atletico Madrid in the summer of 2024.

He wasn't picked up by a European team, so Corinthians offered him a two-year deal in September of that year.

It has been a successful spell in Depay's career, with the Dutchman claiming three trophies while in Brazil.

His arrival to the club saw Corinthians embark on an incredible winning run as they put together nine consecutive victories to end the season.

Depay scored seven times in just 11 appearances to propel Corinthians into the new season.

3 Depay will now be looking for a new club Credit: Getty

The following year, Depay was hit with injury and didn't manage too many league appearances as Corinthians finished tenth.

However, he scored in the final of Copa do Brasil as Corinthians beat Vasco da Gama to claim the trophy.

Last year, injuries really hit Depay, so he barely played at all, making just eight league appearances.

However, he is now fit and was expecting to remain with the Brazilian giants.

Sports.title: Roberto Martinez in secret talks over top international job just weeks after quitting Portugal job
Sports.content:
Roberto Martinez in secret talks over top international job just weeks after quitting Portugal job

Roberto Martinez is being lined up to become the Netherlands' first foreign manager of the national team in 48 years.

The 53-year-old is out of a job having stepped down as Portugal boss following their World Cup exit last month.

3 Martinez could be poised to become manager of a third different national team Credit: Getty

Despite his contract expiring at the end of July, Martinez immediately left his role after Portugal lost 1-0 to Spain in the last-16.

He was one of 17 managers that left their position as head coach either during the global tournament in North America, or after their run in the competition concluded.

The Netherlands are one of those countries that are now on the lookout to fill their vacancy.

Ronald Koeman called time on his three-and-a-half-year spell in charge after Holland lost to Morocco on penalties in the round of 32 stage.

Who could replace Koeman for the Netherlands?

As first reported by De Telegraaf, former Everton and Wigan boss Martinez, who has also been linked with the Scotland job, could be the man to replace him.

It has been said that the Spaniard has held talks with KNVB technical director Nigel de Jong over the position.

The report also claims that Arne Slot, Erik ten Hag and Peter Bosz have all passed up on the chance to take over from Koeman.

Former Liverpool manager Slot has signalled his intention to remain in club football.

He said: "At this stage of my career, I prefer to see myself on the training pitch with my players every day.

"Something that is simply not possible in the same way with a national team."

3 Slot has declared he wishes to remain in club football before looking towards an international job Credit: Getty

Before adding: "For now, I believe that club football still has a lot to offer me."

Meanwhile, despite Louis van Gaal publicly stating his desire to manage Holland for a fourth time, the KNVB have not contacted him.

De Jong is alleged to have now turned to Martinez, with his potential appointment to be a historic one.

Austrian Ernst Happel was the last non-Dutchman to be in charge of the national team - lasting just 12 games between August 1977 and June 1978.

But in Martinez, they have a boss who boasts a wealth of experience in national team football, with the ex-Wigan midfielder not managing a club since leaving Goodison Park in May 2016.

He spent six-and-a-half-years with Belgium, who he notably took to the World Cup semi-finals in 2018.

3 Martinez is on the lookout for a new job having stepped down at Portugal - a role he lasted three-and-a-half-years in Credit: Getty

While he guided Portugal to Nations League glory in 2025 from his three-and-a-half-years in charge.

Known to get itchy feet without a job, Martinez has never spent more than two months and eight days without a role since landing his first managerial gig at Swansea in February 2007.

What has been said about Martinez managing the Netherlands?

Despite reports that Martinez could replace Koeman, his lawyer Jesse de Preter pointed out the fact they tend to not appoint foreign managers.

Seemingly playing down the link, he told Voetbal International: "If Nigel de Jong calls, we will enter into talks.

"But traditionally the KNVB go for a Dutch coach and financially I suspect the expectations are very far apart.

"I do not see how this can become a deal."

Sports.title: Gladiators legend and ex-England star John Fashanu hits out at his 'soon-to-be ex-wife' in family feud as he apologises to his daughter and threatens 'legal action against the liar'
Sports.content:
Gladiators legend and ex-England star John Fashanu hits out at his 'soon-to-be ex-wife' in family feud as he apologises to his daughter and threatens 'legal action against the liar'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Former England footballer and Gladiators legend John Fashanu has publicly apologised to his daughter and revealed he is divorcing his wife in a scathing statement.

In a lengthy Instagram post, Fashanu, who presented the TV show for six seasons in the 1990s when he became associated with the catchphrase 'Awooga', took a brutal swipe at his 'soon-to-be ex-wife' and regretted spreading misinformation about his daughter, Amal.

Fashanu said: 'I’m here to clarify a few things, very important things. The video I previously did was wrong.

'I was misinformed by my wife Vivian, who I’m sorry to say I am divorcing. Now that I am aware of the truth I apologise to my daughter Amal and legal action will be taken against the liar.'

Fashanu was speaking to camera in the post, which was captioned: 'I was the one who called my daughter, Amal, to become involved in my business because she is my first daughter, and she has always held a very special place in my heart.

'Sadly, I allowed myself to be misinformed and influenced. My soon-to-be ex-wife, Vivian, created unnecessary division between me and my daughter, and I deeply regret allowing that to happen.'

John Fashanu has apologised to his daughter Amal and revealed he is divorcing his wife

Speaking more about their feud, the former Wimbledon star continued: 'Amal, I want to publicly say I’m sorry for that previous video. It was made at a time when I was listening to someone else’s anger instead of following my own heart.

'The truth is, Amal and I have a wonderful relationship. She will always be my first daughter, and she will always have a place by my side, helping me with my affairs.

'I couldn’t be prouder of the intelligent, strong and compassionate woman she has become. What makes me even prouder is that she never chose to retaliate. As she always says, "Two wrongs don’t make a right".

'Those words have stayed with me, and they say everything about the kind of person she is.'

The 63-year-old, who has been married three times, also insisted that 'life is too short for division' and that 'family is everything', before he hinted that he and his daughter are trying to repair things.

His latest post comes after Fashanu had bizarrely denied claims Amal made about him earlier this summer.

Fashanu apologised to his daughter Amal (pictured together in 2012) for how he had acted

Former footballer Fashanu presented Gladiators in the early 1990s alongside Ulrika Jonsson

She had said that they had reconciled ahead of her wedding and hoped that he would attend, but added he had been 'laid low by a mystery condition'.

Fashanu, however, refuted these claims and instead insisted his daughter was trying to defame him.

During his football career, the 63-year-old played for several clubs but was most associated with Wimbledon where he scored more than 100 goals and won the 1988 FA Cup.

After retiring due to injury in his early 30s, he presented Gladiators alongside Ulrika Jonsson.

Sports.title: Brennan Johnson hits back at Jamie O'Hara and Gabby Agbonlahor after pair poked fun at swap deal with Dwight McNeil: 'We'll give you c**p, we'll give you c**p back!'
Sports.content:
Brennan Johnson hits back at Jamie O'Hara and Gabby Agbonlahor after pair poked fun at swap deal with Dwight McNeil: 'We'll give you c**p, we'll give you c**p back!'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Brennan Johnson has clapped back at Jamie O'Hara and Gabriel Agbonlahor after the pair mocked his latest transfer.

Johnson has joined Everton in a swap deal from Crystal Palace with Dwight McNeil going the other way.

Johnson's time in south-east London was brief, having only moved to the club in January from London rivals Tottenham.

Following confirmation of the transfer on Tuesday, O'Hara and Agbonlahor discussed the details while speaking on talkSPORT.

'I like Dwight McNeil,' O'Hara said during the discussion. 'Brennan Johnson has been a myth for a few seasons. He didn't do it at Spurs. He hides in games.'

Agbonlahor then chimed in with: 'You look at their output last season, it's a bit like "you give us him and we'll give you him!"'

😅 "Give us crap, we'll give you crap back!"



🤷‍♂️ "I like Dwight McNeil but Brennan Johnson has been a myth!"



O'Hara and Agbonlahor react to #CPFC and #EFC swapping Dwight McNeil and Brennan Johnson! 🔁 pic.twitter.com/Avc4VcR7y1 — talkSPORT (@talkSPORT) August 11, 2026

Brennan Johnson has hit out at Jamie O'Hara and Gabby Agbonlahor for their remarks about his output after joining Everton in a swap deal with Dwight McNeil going to Crystal Palace

O'Hara (top) and Agbonlahor (bottom) mocked the output of Johnson and McNeil (right)

I have to say, I rate Brennan Johnson for pushing back against them with this reply. He didn’t do it in our colours admittedly but it’s good to see him standing up for himself. https://t.co/jTA8Lhyf4J pic.twitter.com/MvlmGor8t3 — HLTCO (@HLTCO) August 12, 2026

As the duo laughed, O'Hara then threw in another jab, commenting: 'We'll give you crap, we'll give you crap back!'

Johnson though, hit back at the pair on Instagram, writing under the post: 'Won more than both of these put together.'

And the Wales international is not lying, having won two major trophies so far compared to the one combined between his two critics.

O'Hara won the 2007-08 League Cup with Tottenham, while Agbonlahor won nothing during his career. However, Johnson scored the winning goal in the Europa League final in 2024-25 for Tottenham and won the Europa Conference League with Palace last season.

Following criticism of his comments, O'Hara took to X on Wednesday to defend himself, writing: 'This the prob [problem] when you only listen to a clip and not full story.

'We were talking about Brennan and McNeil stats from last season which were C**P not that they were bad players, I'm a fan of McNeill [sic] and also said Brennan has all the attributes but he would admit his season was crap.'

Agbonlahor was on talkSPORT again on Wednesday morning and apologised for any outburst, directing the blame from O'Hara.

'What did I do wrong? It was Jamie that said 'c**p for c**p,'' Agbonlahor said tongue-in-cheek.

this the prob when you only listen to a clip and not full story,we were talking about Brennan and McNeil stats from last season which were CRAP not that they were bad players, I’m a fan of McNeill and also said Brennan has all the attributes but he would admit his season was crap — Jamie Ohara (@Mrjamieohara1) August 12, 2026

🤷 "What did i do wrong?!"

❌ "I thought Jamie O'Hara was out of order."



Gabby Agbonlahor forced to apologise to Brennan Johnson after he responded to his comments on Instagram 🔥#talkSPORT #BrennanJohnson pic.twitter.com/4CD4qFlAyP — talkSPORT (@talkSPORT) August 12, 2026

'I want to apologise to Brennan Johnson. I could have not laughed, but when someone makes you laugh it's normal to start laughing.

'I thought Jamie O'Hara was out of order. I think Jamie needs to apologise. You can't say 'cr*p for cr*p'. I thought Jame was out of order looking back at that now.'

Sports.title: Why 'overloaded' Youri Tielemans believes he can be Man United's marathon man: £35m star speaks for first time on Michael Carrick, beating Lionel Messi's record and Bruno Fernandes link-up
Sports.content:
Why 'overloaded' Youri Tielemans believes he can be Man United's marathon man: £35m star speaks for first time on Michael Carrick, beating Lionel Messi's record and Bruno Fernandes link-up

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

When Youri Tielemans made his professional debut for Anderlecht against Lokeren, Michael Carrick, now his boss, still had five years left to run on his own playing career at Manchester United. That goes some way to underline Tielemans' longevity at the top.

Tielemans was a phenomenon in Belgium when he made his pro debut in 2013 aged 16. Only Lamine Yamal made double figures Champions League appearances at a younger age than Tielemans, who had achieved that by the time he was 17. At 18, he’d played more than 100 professional matches.

Now, at 29, with 668 career appearances in the legs, Tielemans is facing the very real prospect of surpassing Lionel Messi (701), and possibly Cristiano Ronaldo (720), for the most games played before he turns 30.

A return to the Champions League means United face a minimum 48-game season. The more likely number is somewhere in the mid-50s.

And so by the time a trip to Bournemouth comes on the final weekend of the season, Tielemans could well have cruised past Messi’s record. Deep runs in the cups and Ronaldo may be sweating too.

With that in mind, meet Manchester United’s new marathon man.

Youri Tielemans' longevity at the top since making his debut has been remarkable

The midfielder, still only 29, has made 668 career appearances already

Tielemans cannot stop smiling as he sits down to chat inside United’s five-star team base for this week’s training camp in Ireland.

There is plenty on the agenda: his first phone call with Carrick, his ‘really natural’ link-up with Bruno Fernandes, and also an insight into the role he expects to play for United this season.

But first it’s the issue of minutes, of wear and tear, and whether he can be counted on for what, if all goes to plan, could be a 60-odd game campaign for United.

‘Yes, I am [confident],’ he says defiantly. ‘I feel very good, actually. I had a little issue during the World Cup, which is sorted now, and I feel back 100 per cent fit.

‘Obviously, pre-season is all about building up fitness for the season, but, yeah, I feel great. I feel like I am ready to go, and in 10 days’ time [against Hull] we will be there.’

Tielemans is refreshingly honest. Thirteen years as a professional will do that.

He doesn’t shy away from the fact that he missed 21 games for Aston Villa last season through ankle and calf problems. Nor does he gloss over the fact he clocked up 62 appearances during a gruelling 2024-25 season.

At the World Cup this summer, Tielemans reached a limit that his body could not fight against.

‘It was just that last game,’ he explains. ‘It was just an overload of too many games, too many minutes, and unfortunately my body could not cope with it anymore.’

Tielemans senses a shift in the room as he, plainly, recounted Belgium’s final act in the United States.

But he knows his game, he knows his body, and where others hold reservations, he has trust and belief that, after signing a five-year contract, he’s still got plenty left in the tank.

‘The thing is, at the World Cup, I think we played 120 minutes against Senegal, and from there we had less time in between games,’ he continues.

‘So we played the US I think three or four days later, and then three days later we played against Spain. In the warm-up, my body just switched off for some reason.

Tielemans is part of the United squad on their pre-season tour of Ireland this month

‘Now, I do not think I am a player that I absolutely need a rest. Obviously, there is a lot of games and the manager needs to manage the team, but when I am good, I am good, you know… it does not happen often.’

There is a steeliness in Tielemans eyes that is befitting of someone who plays for a club the size of Manchester United. A club that, had things shaken out differently, he could have turned out for as early as 2019 when he was first approached.

That was when he was leaving Monaco, only for Tielemans end up at Leicester.

United came back in for him again in the summer of 2022, only to end up signing Casemiro and Christian Eriksen in central midfield instead. Tielemans would have been forgiven for thinking the opportunity to head to Old Trafford may have passed him by.

So, now he’s here, replacing the void left by Casemiro, does he feel any sense of pressure at stepping into the Brazilian’s shoes?

‘Not really, because we are all different players,’ Tielemans adds. ‘He has different qualities, he had a different career path than I have. I just try to be myself, to bring my own qualities to the team, and to enjoy my time here. But it does not add any pressure at all for me.’

At £35million, a release clause which we now know had been hiding in plain sight to the rest of the league, he is a bargain that those inside Manchester United believe could prove to be the pound-for-pound the league’s most valuable signing of the summer.

He played a central role in helping Aston Villa - a club he says he ‘owes the world’ for restoring him to his best level - win the Europa League against Freiburg in Istanbul and has the Premier League proven tag that Ineos and United hold in such high regard.

Beyond just the numbers, United have been crying out for a rhythm-setter. A metronome who can help the team control matches. In his own words, it’s the ‘smelling football’ philosophy Carrick is hoping to have Tielemans bring.

‘He wants to have the ball, he wants to press in certain ways,’ Tielemans explains, revealing one of his early tactical conversations with Carrick.

‘It might be different than what you are used to, what I have been used to before, but it is logical things in my opinion. It is just smelling football, and that is what I have been doing from when I was young at Anderlecht. So for me, nothing changes.

‘But it just needs to gel together. When you follow those principles, then you can add your offensive qualities, especially in the last third where everything is a bit more about freedom, without obviously overcommitting and keeping the defensive line in place. Then I think we can do good things.’

Having played as a deep-lying defensive No 6, a box-to-box No 8 and more advanced as a No 10, what does Tielemans see as his best role to help take United back to the top?

The midfielder signed this summer from Aston Villa - a club he says he 'owes the world' to for helping to reignite his career

‘I just try and play forward as much as I can,’ he says, ‘either to Bruno [Fernandes] or the front line, to try and put them in positions that they can attack with freedom and that they can create and use their qualities.

‘I have played different roles in my career. So yeah, I am not just glued to one system or one role. I try and do a bit of everything.

‘Being that link between the defence and the attack, I think that suits me the best.’

He will be a key mentor in a young group, too, alongside the likes of Tyler Fletcher (19), Kobbie Mainoo (21) and fellow new signing Andrey Santos (22).

‘I just try to be myself, and it all comes in a natural way,’ Tielemans concludes.

‘I do not try to boss anyone around because no one likes that anyway. So I just try to be myself, be natural, and then obviously with good performances it helps others to follow.’

Leading by example at the very top level is all Tielemans has known for the past 13 years. It’s why Messi, Ronaldo, a place in the record books, and the game’s biggest prizes, are all in his sights now he’s finally here at Manchester United.

Sports.title: Why Crystal Palace cut their losses on Brennan Johnson - despite team-mates wanting him to stay: His eye-watering salary, the problem Oliver Glasner identified and Palace insiders' instant regret
Sports.content:
Brennan Johnson, the second-most expensive signing in Crystal Palace history, has been shipped off to Everton in an unusual swap deal with Dwight McNeil heading the other way.

Johnson joined Palace in early January for £35million, a club-record fee trumped only by Jorgen Strand Larsen a few weeks later. Around the same time they landed Strand Larsen, Palace agreed a £15million deal for McNeil, before pulling the plug at the 11th hour.

Yet, seven months later, McNeil is a Palace player and Johnson is an Everton player despite no money changing hands. How did we get here?

Well, McNeil had one year remaining on his contract at Everton, while Johnson had four years left to run at Palace. Both players had been valued in January, at £15million and £35million respectively.

Take the housing market. If someone has their house valued at £500,000, they don’t accept an offer for £100,000 seven months later - unless the market crashes.

The football transfer market is more inflated than ever, and Palace have essentially acknowledged they overspent on Johnson in January by proceeding with this deal.

Brennan Johnson won the Conference League at Crystal Palace, but did little to contribute - failing to score in 26 appearances after joining in January

Swapping him for a £15million asset accepts a £20million loss, certainly in cash-flow terms. There are some clever accounting mechanisms to limit the brutal hit on the books. But even so, it is cash Palace will never see again – just seven months after investing.

They have, however, offloaded a top earner, with Johnson’s Palace salary thought to be £125,000 a week. McNeil is understood to be on significantly less. That frees up some much-needed funds.

Where did it all go wrong?

When Johnson spoke ahead of last season’s Conference League final, there remained a sense that all was not lost for him in a Crystal Palace shirt.

Despite a dismal start to life at Selhurst Park, Johnson was introspective in a bumper 17-minute interview.

Five Palace players spoke that day, but Johnson stuck around significantly longer than his counterparts. He was optimistic and portrayed his move to Palace as the right decision, even after a disappointing, goalless four months.

Yet behind that mask was a man without any self-belief. Damaged by a difficult half-season under Thomas Frank at Tottenham Hotspur, Johnson had seen his minutes limited despite being Spurs’ key man the previous season – scoring 18 goals in a campaign that ended in Europa League glory.

At Spurs, Johnson went from top dog to a player largely frozen out. From the highest point of his career, scoring the winner in a European final, to the lowest, all in a matter of months.

Brennan Johnson scored the winning goal in the 2025 Europa League final, but Ange Postecoglou's exit as Spurs boss saw his minutes drop

A fresh opportunity in January was welcomed, with Palace keen to bolster their forward options for the culmination of their Conference League campaign. In the end, however, it was a mistake.

The first problem for the 25-year-old was his incompatibility with Palace’s style of play. Johnson is an out-and-out winger. He thrives when starting wide, making lung-busting runs from the touchline before eventually finding himself in space at the far post. It is his trademark move.

But at Palace, he was shoehorned into a narrow position, playing as a No 10 – a role he had no experience of – meaning he rarely had the opportunity to showcase what he does best.

Then Palace boss Oliver Glasner felt he was overburdening himself, and his performances were floundering as a result.

‘I feel sometimes he puts himself under too much pressure so that he doesn't play with this freedom that maybe he should have,’ Glasner said in March.

‘He just should enjoy playing football because he’s such a great player. He has all the skills. With freedom I think then he will be the best version of himself and have his best performances.’

But as the weeks went on, his confidence continued to plummet. Johnson missed a crucial penalty in Wales’ World Cup qualification play-off against Bosnia in March, and he never recovered.

Johnson never got going at Selhurst Park and played like a player with very little confidence

There was rarely any conviction behind his actions on the pitch. That is not to say he was not trying; rather, he did not back himself.

There was a consistent absence of end product from the Welshman, who occasionally ventured into promising positions but stopped short of delivering the final ball or applying the finishing touch.

His performances were insipid – averaging just 1.72 dribbles per 90 minutes, 3.08 touches in the opposition box per 90 and losing possession 13.12 times per 90.

There was very little Johnson did well in a Palace shirt, which is not necessarily an indictment of his ability.

He showed more in training than he ever did in a game. Daily Mail Sport understands several Palace players wanted Johnson to remain at the club because they believed in his talent – from glimpses on the training pitch – and just felt he needed reassuring.

But members of the hierarchy are thought to have been unconvinced early on and were worried that they had misspent £35million.

As his wait to end his goal drought dragged on, his head continued to drop. The outside noise also increased, with supporters becoming irritated by his lack of output. Palace travel to his new club Everton on the opening day of the Premier League season, and Johnson will hope to prove those doubters wrong immediately.

How did the swap deal come about?

By the summer, Palace accepted he was the wrong fit and decided to cut their losses, with Johnson equally keen to find a new challenge. That presented an opportunity to Everton, who were among the potential suitors in January.

Toffees boss David Moyes has long been an admirer of Johnson, tracking him since his days at Nottingham Forest – he even tried to sign him while West Ham boss.

The club were amazed by Palace’s generous terms and negotiated a straight swap for McNeil. But it has been suggested that both Palace and Johnson believed it was best for him to move on, paving the way for a rare swap deal. The pair also share the same agency, Unique Sports Group.

David Moyes has finally got his man, having chased Johnson while West Ham boss

Merseyside may prove a more suitable landing spot for Johnson, playing in a familiar system and role, back on the right wing. He will be encouraged to embark on those wide runs that were rarely seen in a Palace shirt.

Moyes, too, is a good manager for wounded animals. Last season he rejuvenated Jack Grealish after a tough spell at Manchester City. He did similarly for Jesse Lingard at West Ham. The Scot will back himself to unearth the attacker that showed so much promise at Nottingham Forest and in his first two seasons at Spurs.

For Everton, there is little risk, aside from his hefty wages. They have acquired a player with a track record of delivering goals and assists – Palace aside – but one in desperate need of nurturing and guidance. All they needed to do was sacrifice McNeil, who they had been prepared to sell for some time.

Sports.title: Chelsea sign Marc Cucurella replacement, Aston Villa line up move for West Ham star while Newcastle press on with pursuit of Benfica defender: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Palace set to sell another youngster

Belgian top-flight side Cercle Brugge are working on a six-figure deal to sign Tayo Adaramola from Crystal Palace.

The 22-year-old Palace academy product is in the final year of his contract, having spent six loan spells away from the club since 2022 and impressed at Sheffield Wednesday in the second half of last season.

Adaramola made his senior international debut this year, starting in the Republic of Ireland’s 5-0 win over Grenada in May.

He is expected to become the third academy player sold this summer, with Mofe Jemide set to join Alverca after Danny Imray joined Wrexham for £5million.

EXCLUSIVE BY BOBBY MANZI

Chelsea sign Marc Cucurella replacement

Chelsea have signed Rayo Vallecano left-back Pep Chavarria on a five-year deal for a fee of around £16.3m plus add-ons.

The 28-year-old replaces Marc Cucurella, who signed for Real Madrid earlier this summer in a £55.8m deal.

After signing his five-year deal, Chavarria told club media: 'I'm so excited to get started.

'This is a dream for me as Chelsea are one of the biggest clubs in the world. This is one of the best days of my life,' added the 28-year-old.

'It is a big opportunity but I am prepared and will work hard to help the team achieve success.

'There are a lot of people who have helped me get to this moment and I have to thank my family. They have always supported me and today is only possible because of them.'

Chelsea have signed Rayo Vallecano left-back Pep Chavarria on a five-year deal

Toon press on with Benfica target

Newcastle United are pressing ahead with talks to sign Amar Dedic from Benfica.

The 23-year-old right-back played for new Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle at RB Salzburg.

Dedic has been capped 31 times by Bosnia and is valued around £25m.

Newcastle continue to work on a new midfielder too.

Camara never lies

Crystal Palace have held further talks with Monaco over 22-year-old midfielder Lamine Camara.

The clubs have been discussing a £40million deal for the Senegal international who has also been tracked by Chelsea, Newcastle and Manchester United.

Camara impressed in Monaco's friendly against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

Monaco are understood to want a fee in excess of £50m for the midfielder who has three years left on his contract.

Palace have also spoken about France international Youssouf Fofana who is available from AC Milan.

Villa Wan him

Aston Villa are discussing a move for West Ham right-back Aaron Wan-Bissaka.

The 28-year-old is ready to leave West Ham to stay in the top flight and has been considered as a new addition by a number of clubs including Arsenal but Villa are understood to be in pole position.

The Congo international has also been linked with Everton but manager David Moyes is exploring other options.

Aston Villa are discussing a move for West Ham defender Aaron Wan-Bissaka

Villa are in the process of signing Matteo Ruggeri from Atletico Madrid to strengthen their left back options and now Wan-Bissaka looks a strong option for their right-back berth.

They have previously discussed Emerson Royal at Flamengo.

The Eagle has landed... again!

Evann Guessand has rejoined Crystal Palace on a season-long loan from Aston Villa.

Guessand spent the second half of last season on loan at Selhurst Park, playing 14 times as Palace won the UEFA Conference League.

Palace chose not to exercise his option to buy at the end of last season’s loan but remained open to the possibility of Guessand returning on loan. This switch also includes an option to buy.

Palace initially chased the Ivorian on a permanent deal last summer, but he opted to join Aston Villa - where he made just 21 appearances - in a £30million deal from Nice.

Rejoining Palace, Guessand said: ‘I'm so happy to be here. I already have good memories here – but I think it's only the beginning. I hope many more are coming.’

BOBBY MANZI

Spurs youngster heading to Belgium

Tottenham winger Yang Min-Hyeok has joined KVC Westerlo in Belgium on loan for the 2026/27 season.

Yang, 20, signed for Spurs in July 2024 but completed the season in South Korea and moved to London in January 2025. He has been on loan at QPR, Portsmouth and Coventry.

Spurs have a close relationship with Westerlo. Alfie Devine and Luka Vuskovic are among those who have been loaned there.

MATT BARLOW

City land Geronimo

Manchester City have signed goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli from Marseille for £1.7million.

The 34-year-old Argentina international has signed a two-year deal and provides cover after James Trafford was sold to Leeds for £40m plus £5m in add ons.

Rulli spent the 2016-17 season at City without making a first-team appearance, playing on loan at Real Sociedad.

Manchester City have signed goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli from Marseille for £1.7million

Till Douath do us part

Hull City have agreed a deal with RB Salzburg to sign midfielder Lucas Gourna-Douath in a permanent move worth £3.5m.

The 23-year-old is travelling to Hull for a medical.Sunderland had also shown interest.

The France U21 international has one year left on contract at Salzburg and impressed in the second half of last season with a spell on loan at Le Havre where he was instrumental in them avoiding relegation.

Wolf at the door for Jordan James

Wolves are closing on a £10million deal for Rennes midfielder Jordan James.

The 22-year-old Wales international had interest from Middlesbrough and West Ham also.

He impressed on loan at Leicester City last season scoring 11 goals in 34 games.

James first shot to prominence when he started out at neighbouring Birmingham City.

Sports.title: How Jose Mourinho destroyed relationship with Cristiano Ronaldo and made Real Madrid dressing room a 'hellhole': Iker Casillas hits out at former boss after explosive first spell at the Bernabeu
Sports.content:
How Jose Mourinho destroyed relationship with Cristiano Ronaldo and made Real Madrid dressing room a 'hellhole': Iker Casillas hits out at former boss after explosive first spell at the Bernabeu

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Jose Mourinho's fallout with the Real Madrid dressing room has been laid bare in the new documentary about his career.

Mourinho returned to the Bernabeu this summer, 13 years after his turbulent first stint came to a close.

During that three-year spell, the legendary Portuguese boss clashed with several senior players, including club captain Iker Casillas.

And in a new Netflix documentary Mourinho, released earlier this week, further light has been shed on just what happened.

In the show, Mourinho was asked about his relationship with Casillas, who he had originally labelled as the 'captain and best player' upon his arrival.

'Mentally, they were in a very bad place,' he said of Real's squad. 'The first thing he (Casillas) told me was: "I've come to ask for more vacation time for the national team players".

Jose Mourinho and Iker Casillas have opened up on how their relationship fell apart

Mourinho's fallout with Casillas also impacted his relationship with Real star Cristiano Ronaldo

'In the second conversation, he asked me to delay training by an hour because there was a lot of traffic in Madrid at the time I wanted to start the session.

'In the third, he told me they didn't want to go to the hotel, that they preferred to see each other on match day and go directly to the stadium.'

Following these conversations, Mourinho added: 'I realised they were being spoiled.'

From this moment, Mourinho's relationship with Casillas continued to deteriorate, with one particular flashpoint coming when the keeper called Xavi to ease tensions between the Spanish players at Real Madrid and Barcelona.

This came at a time when the El Clasico rivalry was particularly fierce while Mourinho and Pep Guardiola were in charge of either team.

'This is a Barcelona-Real Madrid match,' Mourinho added. 'When you're with the national team, you can kiss each other twice, but not now. This is war.

'There are things I don't accept and never will. When someone doesn't respect me, it becomes a problem.'

Explaining the reasons for the call, Casillas, who was interviewed for the documentary, explained: 'That situation was complicated because you were captain of Real Madrid and captain of the Spanish national team.

'You were facing team-mates who were your enemies on the football field, but then they were your team-mates on the national team. I didn't like seeing that and I told the manager.'

Reflecting how their conflict erupted, with Mourinho later dropping Casillas, former Real midfielder Sami Khedira added: 'Iker was a Real Madrid legend, beloved by the fans.

'Mourinho benched him and wouldn't speak to him, spoke ill of him in the media... the dressing room became a hellhole.

'After that, the relationship between Jose and many players, like Cristiano Ronaldo and the Spanish players, broke down. And those players were very important to the atmosphere in the dressing room, which became poisoned.'

Mourinho also later suspected Casillas was a dressing room 'mole', leaking line-ups, tactics and internal secrets to the media.

Mourinho is now back at Real and a documentary about his career was released this week

Speaking at the end of that first spell, Mourinho had opened up on why it had come to an end.

'I think the players had grown tired of me as a leader, and I of them too,' he said. 'I was fed up with them as well, not just them with me.

'I was fed up with the players and the press. I wanted to leave. I felt I was finished.'

Sports.title: Liverpool supporters group calls for 'clarity' on Jeff Bezos' plans for the club as billionaire Amazon founder closes in on securing a minority stake
Sports.content:
Liverpool supporters group calls for 'clarity' on Jeff Bezos' plans for the club as billionaire Amazon founder closes in on securing a minority stake

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Liverpool supporters group Spirit of Shankly have asked the club to offer clarity on what a proposed investment by a group of billionaires including Jeff Bezos would mean for fans.

Amazon founder Bezos, the third-richest man in the world, is part of a consortium closing in on buying a 30 per cent stake worth around £1.35billion, alongside Facebook co-owner Eduardo Saverin and former Queens Park Rangers supremo Amit Bhatia.

While it would have a positive impact on cash-flow for Reds owners Fenway Sports Group, who would still hold the keys to the club, fans have questioned what it means for the long-term future.

Spirit of Shankly published a statement which read: ‘Following initial reports of a potential sale of a stake in LFC, Spirit of Shankly wrote to the club at the end of July seeking further information and greater clarity of what it would mean should a sale go ahead.

‘We asked: when is the ownership expecting to conclude a potential sale? What will the purchasers get in return – board seats, level of involvement in the control of the club on and off the pitch, dividends or other financial returns?

Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, the third-richest man in the world, is part of a consortium closing in on buying a 30 per cent stake worth around £1.35billion in Liverpool

Supporters group Spirit of Shankly have called on current owners FSG to explain what the investment means for the club in the long-term

‘Is this part of a planned wider sale, or a one-off? What is the reasoning for FSG considering such a sale?

‘What due diligence is being done on the potential investors/owners? This is about their plans, reasons for purchase and involvement in sports or business elsewhere.

‘We also asked for a meeting and reiterated that, given the events that led to FSG’s purchase of the club, who owns it and how they control it – putting the interests of LFC and its supporters first – is fundamental to us all.

‘The latest report of a 30 per cent sale and the consortium set up to buy it is significant. The ownership and custodianship of our club is paramount to SOS and all supporters.

‘We have witnessed similar sales at other clubs resulting in notable changes in the running of that club and football operations, leading to decisions and behaviours that many would not want to see at Liverpool.’

The club told Spirit of Shankly they would meet the supporters’ board if and when things become more formal.

Sources close to the deal and FSG both insist talks remain ongoing but no deal has been struck yet.

Sports.title: Former Man United star accuses Corinthians of 'unacceptable' behaviour after they decide against renewing his contract
Sports.content:
Former Man United star accuses Corinthians of 'unacceptable' behaviour after they decide against renewing his contract

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Memphis Depay has hit out at his former club Corinthians for their 'unacceptable behaviour' at not honouring an alleged agreement between both parties for him to sign a new contract at the club.

The former Manchester United, Barcelona and Atletico Madrid forward joined the Brazilian outfit on a two-year deal in 2024.

He is now a free agent and has accused Corinthians of reneging on a contract extension until 2028 for him.

'Very disappointed to read that Corinthians decided not to honour our agreement in place to extend my contract for two more years,' the Netherlands international wrote on social media.

'This renewal was explicitly agreed upon by the president as well as the sporting, legal and financial department. Some people decided however to breach this engagement.

'I didn't want this situation and always respected the club throughout the process, but now I am forced to react strongly in order to preserve my interests.

Very disappointed to read that Corinthians decided not to honour our agreement in place to extend my contract for 2 more years. This renewal was explicitly agreed upon by the president as well as the sporting, legal and financial department. Some people decided however to breach… — Memphis Depay (@Memphis) August 12, 2026

Memphis Depay has accused Corinthians of not honouring an agreement to extend his deal

Depay, who helped Copa do Brasil in 2025 and the Supercopa do Brasil this year, says the Brazilian outfit's actions are 'unacceptable' after a two-year extension had been agreed

'In the upcoming days I will speak publicly but rest assured that I will not leave this unacceptable behaviour unsanctioned.'

Depay scored 20 goals in 79 appearances for Corinthians and helped them win the Copa do Brasil in 2025 and the Supercopa do Brasil this year.

Citing why they have decided against extending the 32-year-old's stay, Corinthians pointed toward financial reasons.

'It became clear that taking on a new commitment of this magnitude would not be compatible with the financial balance we need to preserve to ensure the institution's sustainability,' the Sao Paulo-based club - who are seventh in Brazil's Serie A - said in a statement.

'We recognise that this was a difficult decision, but it was undoubtedly necessary for the future of Corinthians.'

The club added that their president, Osmar Stabile, would hold a press conference to address the decision.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino eyes another huge World Cup change to secure position as FIFA chief
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino eyes another huge World Cup change to secure position as FIFA chief

FIFA President Gianni Infantino's future in the role remains uncertain, but is reportedly in favour of expanding the World Cup once again

View 2 Images FIFA president Gianni Infantino

FIFA President Gianni Infantino has reportedly expressed a willingness to support another expansion of the World Cup. It has been suggested that Infantino would be in favour of the tournament increasing from 48 to 64 teams, amid ongoing uncertainty around his future in the job.

‌



The uncertainty followed news which emerged that FIFA had proposals that would have seen them sell shares of the federation’s tournaments to private investors.

‌



The controversial scheme would have affected the men's and women's World Cups, as well as the Club World Cup, but was shelved following a substantial backlash.

‌



Infantino's future as FIFA President has been uncertain ever since the proposals emerged, with UEFA releasing statements outlining their plans to boycott the federation's major tournaments if the plans were still on the table.

Gianni Infantino cornered as three federations pile pressure on under-fire FIFA boss READ MORE :

What lies ahead for Infantino remains to be seen, but a fresh update has now emerged purporting to shed light on his position regarding the next World Cup in 2030.

The Times has reported that Infantino would support expanding the tournament once more to accommodate 64 teams, despite the World Cup already having grown from 32 to 48 teams for this summer's competition in North America.

‌



The report suggests that Infantino travelled to Colombia on Friday to attend the inauguration of the country's new president, Abelardo de la Espriella, where discussions over a potential expansion of the World Cup are said to have taken place.

The 2030 World Cup will once again be shared across multiple nations, with Spain, Portugal and Morocco serving as the primary hosts, while Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay will each stage a single match to mark the competition's 100th anniversary.

View 2 Images US President Donald Trump has offered his support to Gianni Infantino (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

The proposals to expand the World Cup to 64 teams were put forward by CONMEBOL, South America's governing football body, with reports suggesting Infantino is prepared to put his support behind the plans as he looks to secure the backing of more nations to secure his presidency.

With Infantino's position shrouded in uncertainty, US President Donald Trump took to Truth Social on Monday to make his feelings abundantly clear, insisting it would be an error to remove the current FIFA chief.

‌



"FIFA would be making a terrible mistake if, for any reason, they even considered replacing President Gianni Infantino,” Trump wrote.

"He is fantastic, having just presided over the most successful World Cup, by four times, ever presented.

"If he is gone, it will never be as successful or profitable again!"

Sports.title: Manchester City sign £2m goalkeeper who destroyed Man Utd's hopes of European trophy
Sports.content:
Manchester City sign £2m goalkeeper who destroyed Man Utd's hopes of European trophy

Leeds United spent big to take James Trafford to Elland Road as their new No.1 but with Gianluigi Donnarumma in situ at the Etihad, they've turned to an experienced Argentine international for cover

View Image Geronimo Rulli celebrates at the end of the 2021 UEFA Europa League final (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Manchester City have completed the signing of Argentine international Geronimo Rulli in a £2m deal.

‌



The goalkeeper has joined City from Marseille on a two-year-deal that will keep him at the Etihad until 2028. Rulli is expected to provide back-up to No.1 Gianluigi Donnarumma.

‌



The former Ajax and Villarreal star once famously scored in a penalty shootout before making the decisive save, as Villarreal won the 2021 Europa League final against Manchester United. He has won eight caps for Argentina and was part of the squad which won the World Cup in Qatar in 2022.

‌



He said: “This is an amazing opportunity for me - and one I had to grasp. When the chance to join Manchester City comes along you have to go for it. Everyone knows what an impressive club this is. City’s success over a long time has been impressive. Everyone I have spoken to about City said I had to join them because they are a club with incredibly high standards.

"Every professional wants to be in a high-performance environment and I can’t wait to get started because I know I will improve and learn, which is always my main priority. My job now is to train hard, get to know the players and staff and do everything I can to reach my best level."

‌



Cristian Romero nears Tottenham exit as transfer fee agreed amid Arsenal interest READ MORE :

It is a second spell for Rulli at City, having previously spent the 2016-17 season at the club without making an appearance.

Football Director Hugo Viana said “It’s a pleasure to welcome Gerónimo back to the Club. The experience he brings is obvious – he has played at the very highest level for many years.

“I have been really impressed by him during our conversations, a strong desire to join us. It’s clear we are getting a brilliant professional, as well as a top ‘keeper.

Article continues below

“Everyone at City is looking forward to welcoming him back to the Club. The qualities he will bring are ones we need, and together with Gigio and Marcus make a great team. Our goalkeeper coaches are really happy with the group.”

Sports.title: Jeff Stelling predicts Premier League winner, top four and relegated trio in 2026/27 table
Sports.content:
Jeff Stelling predicts Premier League winner, top four and relegated trio in 2026/27 table

The talkSPORT presenter has made some eye-catching predictions ahead of the new season, including a surprise relegation candidate

View 3 Images Jeff Stelling has predicted the Premier League table (Image: talkSPORT)

Jeff Stelling has predicted a Chelsea resurgence in 2026/27 but expects Arsenal to retain their Premier League title. The Blues endured a chaotic 2025/26 campaign, which saw Enzo Maresca leave mid-season.

‌



While they reached the FA Cup final, losing to Manchester City, they slumped to a 10th-place finish and missed out on European football. However, with Xabi Alonso now at the helm, he reckons the Blues will finish second, with City third and Manchester United fourth.

‌



Unless English sides completely flop in Europe, fifth will probably be enough to secure Champions League football, and Stelling expects that spot to be filled by Tottenham Hotspur.

‌



Despite their back-to-back 17th-place finishes, there is real hope of progress under Roberto De Zerbi, who has been well backed in the transfer market this summer.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

The former Soccer Saturday anchor has forecast another difficult campaign for Liverpool under new boss Andoni Iraola. After a poor title defence under Arne Slot, who was promptly sacked, Stelling says the Reds will finish one place lower in sixth and have to settle for Europa League, unless they can win the Champions League.

‌



Cristian Romero nears Tottenham exit as transfer fee agreed amid Arsenal interest READ MORE :

Despite losing a succession of key players, plus head coach Eddie Howe, Stelling has gone for Newcastle to finish seventh, one spot ahead of Europa League holders Aston Villa.

Stelling, who made the predictions on talkSPORT, believes Everton will come ninths and Brighton will round out the top 10, with Leeds United a very satisfactory 11th. Next up are Nottingham Forest, Brentford and Bournemouth.

View 3 Images Stelling is expecting Xabi Alonso to lead a Chelsea turnaround (Image: Eurasia Sport Images, Getty Images)

‌



The Hartlepool United fan reckons Frank Lampard's newly promoted Coventry City will survive - and with a bit to spare - by finishing 15th, just ahead of Sunderland in 16th and Crystal Palace in 17th.

In a surprising prediction, Stelling reckons Fulham, after four seasons in the top flight, will go down, finishing between Ipswich Town in 18th and bottom side Hull City.

View 3 Images Stelling fears a difficult debut season for Andoni Iraola at Liverpool (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

‌

Sports.title: Tyson Fury sent clear message as Kristian Prenga sums up Anthony Joshua power
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury sent clear message as Kristian Prenga sums up Anthony Joshua power

Anthony Joshua defeated Kristian Prenga in preparation for a looming bout with Tyson Fury, and now the Albanian has spoken out about what the Gypsy King will face later this year

View 2 Images Kristian Prenga has spoken out (Image: Khalid Alhaj/MB Media/Getty Images)

Kristian Prenga has admitted he has never felt power like Anthony Joshua's after being knocked out by the British boxing star. AJ sent Prenga to the canvas in just the second round of that bout in a dramatic comeback victory, having been knocked down twice himself.

‌



Joshua, 36, set up a fight later this year with Tyson Fury with the heavyweight goliaths to finally meet for a box office clash. The Gypsy King earned a victory over Mariusz Wach in Thailand just 24 hours ahead of Joshua's win as the pair finally got on a collision course.

‌



Prenga almost pulled off a shock victory over Joshua in the opening minutes. The Albanian's most notable win came against Joey Dawejko in 2024, but the 35-year-old had not lost for nine years and earned stoppages against his other 20 opponents.

‌



Joshua was able to rally against his unfancied opponent to send him to the canvas, and Prenga has admitted it was an unfamiliar experience. Asked if the Olympic gold medalist's power was like nothing he'd felt before, Prenga could only reply in the affirmative.

"Of course, it’s power because it’s the first time I got knocked down in my career, in my life," he said. "I’ve never been knocked down in sparring. It’s the first time. I think he has the power."

Rising star Oleksandr Khyzhniak to fight for first boxing title READ MORE :

Tyson Fury's stance on Anthony Joshua fight venue becomes clear READ MORE :

Prenga's assessment comes after boxing legend Lennox Lewis questioned whether Joshua should be back in action following his performance. The former heavyweight champion has concerns over Joshua's current capabilities.

‌



"Does he really belong in the ring right now?" he told The Ring. "A virtual novice put him on the ground twice in the first round. Is that it, have we seen the last of him? It's not like he's his old self."

Prenga pushed back on the assertion that Joshua is past his best. "It’s not true," he said.

View 2 Images Anthony Joshua knocked out Kristian Prenga (Image: Getty Images)

‌



FOLLOW OUR FIGHTING FB PAGE! Latest boxing and MMA news, analysis and much more via our dedicated Facebook page

"Joshua is a great fighter. He has experience. He has power and I know he went through a lot in his life – as we all know. But it’s not an easy fight for Tyson Fury. I promise you."

The expected bout between Joshua and Fury is already the subject of plenty of controversy over where it will take place. There appears to have been growing momentum toward a fight night in the United States, but Eddie Hearn has suggested he will pull the plug on the fight if it comes to fruition without a contract change.

‌



"Everybody wants to do the fight in New York, apart from Anthony Joshua and me," he told The Punch Podcast. "We're under a huge amount of pressure, and we're being told by Turki Alshikh and those guys - Netflix particularly - 'Look, we really want to do the fight in the US.'

"It's almost not a 'please Eddie,' but like, 'We're partners. We're paying a lot of money. Come on, you have to understand that we need to put the fight where we feel is commercially the best place.'"

"By the way, there might even be a situation where they go ahead and announce it anyway, and you'll probably see me come out quite quickly and say, 'No fight.' Because I promise you, if they announce that fight without an agreement in place to change the venue, there will be no fight, and we ain't bluffing," he added.

Sports.title: Amy Hunt sends warning to rivals as she sets sights on European Championship double
Sports.content:
Amy Hunt sends warning to rivals as she sets sights on European Championship double

Fresh from her breakthrough European 100m gold, Amy Hunt has warned there is no limit to her ambitions as she begins her bid for a second title in the 200m.

View Image Novuna GB & NI Team athlete Amy Hunt celebrates her victory in the Women’s 100m at the European Athletics Championships Birmingham 2026.

Amy Hunt is refusing to put a limit on her ambitions as she prepares for the next step in her quest for continental domination.

‌



The newly crowned European 100m champion goes in the 200m semi-finals tonight, the second of four events she is due to compete in this week. The 24-year-old won her breakthrough World Championship silver over the longer distance in Tokyo last summer and is looking to continue her momentum in her ‘favourite event’.

‌



“I'm someone who doesn't shy away from what she knows she can do,” she said. “I am so proud and so comfortable in myself because I get to see what I do every single day at training.

‌



“I train incredibly hard, and I back myself so incredibly hard, because I do want to be the best. I'm not saying that I'm the best right now, but that's something I aspire to be. I thought it was time to upgrade, and it was definitely a coming of age night for me. Now I am kind of fully established. I have two 100m medals in the last two weeks and one more sub-11 to boot, so I’m very happy.”

Hunt credited the unlikely trio of Megan Thee Stallion, High School Musical and Mamma Mia as key to helping her stay calm in the build-up to her 100m showdown, along with keeping her brain active on Wordle.

‌



The Newark speedster admitted to nerves during the build-up to her opening event of a packed week, with a scheduled 20-minute nap going unslept in. But the home favourite was able to lock in when crunch time arrived.

“As soon as I get to the track, my nerves just disappear,” she said. "I am never terrified. I love my job and this is one of the most fun parts of it. The stage of a final doesn’t intimidate me, and I just knew I had to stay calm and not overthink myself into the goal.

“That was why the Commonwealth Games (in Glasgow) really came in handy for me. That’s why I really wanted to do it, to have that experience of being in front of a home crowd and having that medal expectation, because I've never had that before.”

Sports.title: Paul Pogba set to have contract torn up as injured ex-Man Utd star searches for new club
Sports.content:
Paul Pogba set to have contract torn up as injured ex-Man Utd star searches for new club

Paul Pogba is now understood to be on the lookout for a new team, despite reports claiming the ex-Manchester United midfielder was offered a deal

View 3 Images Paul Pogba's future is uncertain (Image: DARREN STAPLES, AFP via Getty Images)

Ex-Manchester United ace Paul Pogba is on the verge of having his contract torn up by Monaco. Last summer, he signed a two-year contract with the European heavyweights.

‌



However, he may be set for a several month long absence after suffering a hamstring injury during Monaco's recent pre-season tour at St George's Park. It's a huge setback for the World Cup winner, having been handed a four-year ban in February 2024, only for it to be successfully appealed and reduced to 18 months.

‌



Last season, he made six appearances for Monaco and was also in the squad for their recent 3-2 pre-season friendly victory over Liverpool. Now it's being reported the deal may be cancelled.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

The Athletic understands both club and player are in talks about having his contract mutually terminated. Last summer, he put pen to paper on a two-year deal, before going on to make his first football appearance for 26 months the following November.

Man Utd have clear transfer priority after Myles Lewis-Skelly offer READ MORE :

Man Utd ready to open talks over £30m transfer in perfect response to double blow READ MORE :

In total, Pogba has featured just six times for Monaco, with all of those performances coming in Ligue 1 last season. He was also present at Anfield for his side's 3-2 victory over Liverpool on Sunday.

‌



However, he has been absent throughout Monaco's pre-season due to fitness concerns, and with contract termination talks ongoing, his future at the club looks increasingly uncertain, reports the Manchester Evening News. Last month, Monaco CEO Thiago Scuro cast doubt over Pogba's future, suggesting he could depart this summer.

View 3 Images Pogba mase his first appearance in over two years last season (Image: Eurasia Sport Images, Getty Images)

"Maybe he'll leave, yes, maybe he'll stay here, yes," Scuro told a news conference. "That's [Pogba's future] a very complicated subject because we have a lot of respect for Paul. For the person first of all.

‌



"When he first arrived here he was very positive, he worked, he helped the young players. But the truth is that the project didn't go well last season. When we started this project during the summer, the expectations that we had were different to what happened.

"I think now, we must be fair to him, look at his preparation every week, to see how he has progressed, his physical level, his technical level. And after, that will be a decision for the coach. If the coach decides to give him game time or not. That depends completely on performances. We have the summer to see what Paul's level will be.

View 3 Images Pogba's future has been plunged into more uncertainty (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

‌



"With Paul, the relationship has always been open, transparent. If, at a certain time, the player's objectives and the club's are different, we have to talk and find a solution. Performance will give all the answers we need."

Pogba, who rose through the academy at United, returned to Old Trafford for £89.3million in 2016 following a stint at Juventus. He subsequently became a key player for Jose Mourinho and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer throughout his six-year second spell with the Reds, racking up more than 200 appearances along the way.

However, Pogba would eventually depart United for a second time in 2022 when his contract ran out, subsequently rejoining Juventus.

Sports.title: Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle offers bleak reality check - 'This is a vacuum'
Sports.content:
Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle offers bleak reality check - 'This is a vacuum'

Newcastle have undergone a major overhaul this summer, with Matthias Jaissle taking over from Eddie Howe as manager and a series of key players leaving in the transfer window

View 3 Images Matthias Jaissle offered a heavy does of realism (Image: Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images)

Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle has tempered expectations around his side this season in his first press conference after taking over from Eddie Howe.

‌



Jaissle has inherited into a tricky situation on Tyneside following a succession of high-profile exits. Howe walked away after nearly five years in the hot seat, while Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes were sold and Kieran Trippier also departed.

‌



Newcastle banked nearly £250million from those transfers, but have opted to sign young unproven players with potential as replacements. Ewen Jaouen, Bazoumana Toure, Sean Steur, Aladji Bamba and Lukas Hornicek have arrived to work under Jaissle.

‌



The 38-year-old German was hired from Al-Ahli and is under no illusions over the task facing him. "We are in that transition phase," he said. "The players who have left were great characters, great players, experienced players. This is now a vacuum.

Tottenham hold the key to Arsenal transfer after Mikel Arteta changes target READ MORE :

"We have to adjust something in the squad by signing these profile of players, or other players need to step up and fill these positions and these leadership roles.

"We are aware of what we need and the squad that we want. Internally, everyone is aware of that, and we are working on the solutions."

‌



Newcastle saw a move for Marseille midfielder Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg fall through recently and remain on the lookout for experience in the transfer window.

The Magpies finished a disappointing 12th in the Premier League last season under Howe and Jaissle has refused to state their ambitions this season. "This will not happen overnight, especially when you now have such a big transition phase," he said.

View 3 Images Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes left for Arsenal (Image: David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

‌



"You need to have a clear goal of where we want to go to. Then, if you have that synergy with the fans, the players and the staff to go there, then I’m pretty sure it will be a successful story. But we need time now. We can only do our best day by day, breaking it down with the goal long ahead.

"We are ambitious. But it makes no sense to promise you anything, because I don’t know how things look in half a year or one year. What we can control, we will control.

"Cutting the tasks down on a daily basis, doing the best job, and then we go in the right direction - and that is going to be successful."

‌



View 3 Images Matthias Jaissle has a rebuilding job on his hands (Image: Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images)

Jaissle will be a contrast to the reserved Howe on the touchline, with his animated style likely to come to the fore. "I will not change my style because that's my personality," he said.

"On the touchline, I am emotional, but I need to respect the box [technical area] a bit more. I'm a bit scared. I hope in the beginning the referees can maybe close their eyes here and there a little. I need to learn that.

Article continues below

"I had a long touchline in Saudi Arabia, so I think the GPS would be quite high if I had worn it!"

Sports.title: Tottenham hold the key to Arsenal transfer after Mikel Arteta changes target
Sports.content:
Tottenham hold the key to Arsenal transfer after Mikel Arteta changes target

Arsenal are desperate to sign an experienced defender in the summer transfer window to cover for William Saliba, but have found themselves reliant on Tottenham for help

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta wants defensive reinforcements (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Arsenal could find themselves frustrated in the transfer market once again after it emerged that they could need a favour from Tottenham to land their latest target.

Mikel Arteta is keen to bring in an experienced defender this summer, to help provide cover for William Saliba, who will miss the start of the season due to a back injury picked up at the World Cup. They have identified Aston Villa's Ezri Konsa as an option, but his £60million valuation and competition from Liverpool complicates things.

The Gunners have therefore turned their attention to Barcelona defender Jules Kounde, according to reports in Spain. The France international is capable of playing at right-back or centre-back, so would offer tactical flexibility to Arteta.

Sport says Arsenal are monitoring Kounde, who still has four years left on his Barca contract so wouldn't come cheap. It is said that the process has 'stalled' currently, partly due to Kounde's reluctance to leave the Catalan club.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Tottenham could hand Arsenal major transfer boost after opening Folarin Balogun talks READ MORE :

However, Barca reportedly would consider a 'multi-million euro' sale because they need funds to revamp their backline. Hansi Flick's side, who have just loaned out Ronald Araujo to Liverpool, are said to be sounding out possible arrivals should Kounde leave.

Their top target in that eventuality is Tottenham right-back Pedro Porro, whose stock is extremely high after helping Spain win the World Cup. But this is where Arsenal's chances of landing Kounde get even more remote.

Porro recently signed a new contract with Spurs until June 2031 and is a key player for manager Roberto De Zerbi, who has no intention of letting him go. It remains to be seen whether the 26-year-old could have his head turned by Barcelona if they step up their pursuit.

View 3 Images Jules Kounde is a target for Arsenal (Image: Jose Breton/Getty Images)

"Pedro is a very important player for us, who has consistently shown his ability to influence matches in both defensive and attacking situations," De Zerbi said after Porro signed a new deal in June.

"As well as his technical quality, I also love his mentality. Every day he wants to work, to learn and to improve, and these are the characteristics that help players reach the highest level."

Arsenal have already been frustrated in their failure to land Vinicius Junior, who used their interest to negotiate a new contract with Real Madrid. The Gunners have therefore been forced to look for alternatives in attack, with Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez the dream signing.

View 3 Images Pedro Porro's stock is very high after the World Cup (Image: John Todd/Getty Images)

Asked if fans could expect further signings this summer following the £75m capture of Bruno Guimaraes, Arteta replied: "Well that's what we're trying to do. If we have the right player in the market to make us much better, we are very looking forward to that."

Arsenal's defence has been leaky in pre-season, but Arteta has insisted that hasn't increased their desire to sign a defender. "I wouldn't go there just to put it isolated there," Arteta said after losing to Borussia Dortmund

"We conceded some poor goals the other day, some poor goals today. In the way we competed, especially. But that's a very collective responsibility. So we need to improve with the players that we have. And we want to improve for sure."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
