World.title: Omiš Returns to its Pirate Past With a Real Spectacle at Sea on August 18th!
World.content:
August the 11th, 2026 – Located in the very heart of central Dalmatia, Omiš is closely connected to the world of the pirate, and the 18th of August promises an absolute spectacle at sea.

Omiš is set to honour its pirate past on August the 18th after a six year break. Marking its victory over the Venetian Empire from the 13th century, an incredible evening of history, local heritage, fireworks and entertainment awaits. This event is much anticipated and will lure in thousands of spectators keen for a trip back in time to the Omiš of old with the legendary leader of the local pirates, Malduh Kačić, at the helm.

why is this event so important?

If you’ve ever been to Dalmatia (and particularly if you’ve sailed along the heavily indented coastline and islands), you may have asked how the country fared back during the days when marauding pirates ruled the Adriatic. Turning the pages of the history book (a long way) back, we find ourselves in an era where piracy wasn’t nearly as frowned upon as it is today. Back then, it was a legitimate business that only the brave dared try their hand (or sword) at.

Along the heavily indented, cove-ridden rocks of the Dalmatian coast, the tradition of piracy goes back even further. It was noted way back during the reign of the various Illyrian tribes that used to live there before the ethnic Croatians arrived.

a hard lesson for venice…

Across the Adriatic Sea, the mighty and somewhat problematic Venetian Empire was very wary of the pirates from Croatia’s Neretva basin. Dominating Adriatic trade, Venice stacked up its enemies and had good reason to keep looking over its proverbial shoulder.

Indeed, back in 887 AD, a battle near Makarska between the Venetians and the so-called Narentine pirates took place, and during which Venetian Duke Pietro Candiano lost his life and his fleet was sunk to the watery depths below. After this event, the Venetians likely paid dearly for the freedom to travel and trade without encountering problems in the Croatian part of the Adriatic.

That relative ease didn’t last long, as the Omiš pirates (or gusari, if you want to truly go local) began disrupting it. That time period coincided with the rising prominence of the Kačić dynasty during the 12th century. This family didn’t have a tree. It was more like a forest. They were dukes and widely known for their ruthlessness and ruled over a large part of southern and central Dalmatia. Although they were officially the subjects of the Hungarian-Croatian king, they enjoyed plenty of autonomy. They opted to use that by organising professional piracy within their dominion.

keeping up with the Kačić family

This fearsome dynasty controlled the majority of the maritime traffic along the eastern Adriatic coast, and both Venetian and Ragusan (Dubrovnik) merchants had to pay up if they wanted to ensure their safe passage through that part of the sea. Just how far they were willing to go in their efforts to fully control that traffic is best explained by the fact that they were accused of attacking the vessels which took the Crusaders to the Palestine, and that even the Pope Honorius III started a war with the pirates, which he lost.

Every peace agreed upon with the Kačić family and Omiš pirates was short-lived, and it took almost two centuries to defeat them and establish safer passage along the Adriatic coast. The Kačić dynasty was eventually defeated and expelled from Omiš after the Venetians finally got the upper hand in 1287. Piracy lingered on, but it eventually weakened. By the time 1444 rolled around, Omiš ended up entirely occupied by the Venetians, and that marked the end of the tradition of piracy once and for all.

Thankfully, you can now freely sail in Dalmatia without any fear of being plundered, pillaged, or forced to pay for your safe passage, but it wasn’t always so peaceful!

Omiš takes us back to its pirate past on august the 18th

Now we’ve delved into the history of just why pirates are so significant to this part of the Dalmatian coast, we can look at what’s to come. After a six year break, Omiš is finally bringing back its beloved Pirate Battle. If you were to ask most people, they’d argue that it’s by far the Adriatic’s most spectacular historical reenactment, and it couldn’t possibly take place in a more apt location. On Tuesday the 18th of August, the Port of Omiš will shed all signs of modernity and totally transform into an authentic thirteenth-century battlefield.

Old vessels will cut across the water, cannons will drown out the summertime cicadas, swords will be drawn and fireworks will light up the blackness of the night sky above the Cetina canyon’s imposing rock faces. This is so much more than a show by the sea, it’s a living, accurate recreation of the moment when the fearless pirates of Omiš outsmarted the powerful and problematic Venice and cemented their rightful place in Dalmatian and indeed wider Croatian legend.

spectators will watch an ancient pirate battle from a modern setting

The last Pirate Battle took place in 2019, just before the coronavirus pandemic struck. An extremely extensive 15 million euro reconstruction of the Port of Omiš began soon after, forcing the event into a temporary pause. Now, the brand-new pier and seafront promenade are finally complete, offering the perfect stage for one of Croatia’s most atmospheric summer spectacles. You’ll be able to watch this ancient battle from a modern waterfront, witnessing heritage and history blend with modern Omiš in perfect harmony.

The newly renovated port and accompanying waterfront can comfortably host 10,000+ spectators, meaning that you’re guaranteed to find a spot from which you can enjoy the re-enactment and the rest of this marvellous event.

Around 150 costumed participants will take part in the upcoming event, with the local KPU Omiški gusari (Omiš Pirates Association) at the helm (no pun intended). They’ll be joined by allied historical groups from across the rest of Croatia: Kumpanija Vela Luka, the Dubrovački trombunjeri, the Klis Uskoks, Društvo Poljičana Sveti Jure – Priko, Bakar Town Guard 1848 and the Požega Town Guard. The event is being entirely organised by the Omiš Tourist Board, with great care paid both to historical accuracy and as a big “welcome back” to a much loved event.

what we can expect on the evening

The programme is set to begin early so that families with children and history lovers can soak up every moment.

18:30 – Activities for children on the waterfront will take place.

19:15 – A grand parade of all of the historical troops through the ancient streets of Omiš will delight all those gathered.

20:15 – The main event will begin, with the Pirate Battle itself in taking place in the ultra-modern, new port.

celebrations across the town

Immediately after that, the celebrations will continue with a performance by Kumpanija Vela Luka, ceremonial cannon fire from the famous Dubrovački trombunjeri (21:10), a dramatic fire show and an incredible fireworks display that will light up the entire harbour and the surrounding tall cliffs which make this town is instantly recognisable (21:40). Once those cannons eventually do fall silent, the celebrations will move to the Croatian Veterans’ Park. Organised by KPU Omiški gusari, the after-party features local food and drink, demonstrations of traditional crafts and a live concert by the popular band Vigor (21:50).

We can say with confidence that this is certainly the perfect way to bring an unforgettable Omiš summer evening to a close.

here’s a look at 2019’s event to get you prepared!

Should you need further information, look no further than here, and make sure to follow along on Instagram for more fantastic images and videos.

World.title: Supreme Judicial Council President Faiq Zidan to visit Syria
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — President of the Iraqi Supreme Judicial Council, Judge Faiq Zidan, is scheduled to conduct an official visit to Syria on Thursday, August 13, 2026, marking a landmark first-of-its-kind judicial mission to Damascus, according to a senior official source.

The high-level visit aims to hold structured talks with Syrian judicial authorities to address shared legal frameworks, cross-border judicial coordination, counter-terrorism extradition agreements, and legal mechanisms regulating bilateral trade corridors.

World.title: Iraq Transport Ministry reports 95% completion of Development Road designs
World.content:
Baghdad (0iraqiNews.com) — Minister of Transport Wahab Al-Hasani met with the Parliamentary Transport and Communications Committee on Tuesday, August 11, 2026, to review execution milestones across strategic infrastructure projects, including the Development Road, the Grand Fao Port, and national rail modernization.

During the executive session, Al-Hasani presented technical updates on the 1,200-kilometer Development Road Project, confirming that primary design phases are near completion, with railway engineering blueprints reaching 95% and highway transit designs at 85%.

Key Operational Metrics & Project Milestones

Development Road Project: Designs for the 1,200 km transit corridor are nearly complete (95% for railway tracks, 85% for highways). The MOU executed with Turkey serves as a preliminary framework with no current financial or legal obligations.

Grand Fao Port: Submerged tunnel construction reached 86% completion, alongside advanced structural work across five main container berths.

Rail Network Modernization: Ministry teams are actively pursuing the rehabilitation of the Baghdad–Mosul–Rabia railway corridor extending toward the Syrian border.

Maritime Fleet Mobilization: State maritime companies confirmed readiness to deploy Iraqi vessels to transport crude oil and refined petroleum products to support alternative national export strategies.

Administrative & Executive Actions: Al-Hasani confirmed the suspension of Iraqi Airways’ former Director-General and two deputies following an internal investigative audit.

Legislative Alignment: Agreement reached to draft amendments to Transport Law No. 80 of 1983 and establish a joint parliamentary-executive committee holding weekly meetings to update transport regulations.

The meeting highlights Iraq’s strategy to transform into a central logistics bridge connecting the Gulf to Europe, bypassing maritime transit chokepoints.

By pairing the Grand Fao Port’s advancing infrastructure with overland rail links extending north to Turkey and west through the Baghdad–Mosul–Rabia line toward Syria, the Ministry of Transport is laying the groundwork for integrated commercial supply chains across Eurasia.

World.title: MP Abdul Jabbar proposes 145 km pipeline to boost Basra crude to Ceyhan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Independent MP and Secretary-General of the Fao–Zakho Coalition, Amer Abdul-Jabbar, proposed a plan on Wednesday, August 12, 2026, to construct a 145-kilometer oil pipeline link to transport Basra crude north toward Turkey’s Ceyhan terminal.

Abdul-Jabbar stated via social media that the proposed missing link would instantly increase Iraq’s northern export capacity by 150,000 to 300,000 barrels per day (bpd). To avoid drawing on the federal budget during the ongoing liquidity crisis, he advocated launching a “National Volunteer Effort,” utilizing surplus piping from state-owned enterprises alongside logistical backing from private contractors operating under Ministry of Oil contracts.

Key Technical & Strategy Highlights

Proposed Pipeline Link: A 145 km strategic bypass connecting southern oilfields in Basra directly to northern export routes toward the Turkish port of Ceyhan.

Capacity Increase: Designed to boost crude export flows by 150,000 to 300,000 bpd, mitigating bottlenecks caused by Persian Gulf shipping disruptions.

Zero-Cost Volunteer Framework: Proposed execution via a “National Volunteer Effort” using inventory audits of unused piping across state firms and private sector contractor support.

Existing Ministry Export Strategy: Complements Oil Minister Basim Mohammed Khudair’s August 9 plan to export 750,000 bpd to Ceyhan via: 450,000 bpd pumped through the Strategic Pipeline after rehabilitating the PS3 pump station in Najaf and K3 in Haditha. 300,000 bpd transported via road tankers (including 200,000 bpd through KAR Group and 100,000 bpd under a secondary contract).

Long-Term Iraqi-Turkish Energy Framework: Ministry of Oil is finalizing a 1-year interim agreement with Ankara, paving the way for a 10- to 20-year strategic partnership involving Turkish BOTAŞ and BP in developing Kirkuk oilfields.

Abdul-Jabbar’s proposal comes as the Ministry of Oil accelerates alternative land-based export channels to bypass the blocked Strait of Hormuz.

Minister Khudair previously confirmed that Iraq’s State Company for Oil Projects (SCOP) and Turkey’s BOTAŞ are actively inspecting and rehabilitating the northern export system to handle between 500,000 and 750,000 bpd. Implementing the 145 km bypass link could offer Baghdad an immediate, low-cost mechanism to restore crude cash flows while long-term pipeline infrastructure is constructed toward Syria and Jordan.

World.title: Meta meets its own ‘tobacco’ moment in court
World.content:
Oakland – With billions of users around the world, Meta will defend itself against allegations of harming children in a new trial in the United States this week, which experts describe as social media’s big tobacco moment.

After a coalition of states sued Meta in 2023 for allegedly designing addictive features for kids in its apps, four states were selected to represent their claims: California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey.

Top prosecutors of those states now aim to prove in federal court that Meta deliberately made Facebook and Instagram addictive for children.

Meta “strongly disagrees with these allegations” and is “confident the evidence will show our longstanding commitment to supporting young people,” a spokesperson told AFP, adding that the company has “listened to parents, worked with experts and law enforcement.”

Although it’s not the first lawsuit that seeks to hold a social media company accountable for its impact on mental health and safety, it could become one of the most consequential.

“It really feels like tobacco in the 1990s,” Vincent Joralemon, a director at Berkeley’s Life Sciences Law and Policy Center, told AFP.

While these cases about social media harms revolve around the intersection of technology and addiction, the legal argument in this case against Meta centers on its business practices, just like when the federal government sued tobacco companies around three decades ago, Joralemon said.

By the early 1990s, decades of research showed that tobacco use caused health problems such as cancer, and eventually additional investigations revealed how the industry deliberately downplayed, and even concealed, the harmful impacts of its products.

– ‘Protecting teens’ –

Dozens of US states sued four major tobacco companies, and by 1998, won a landmark settlement agreement which included financial penalties and changes to how products were marketed, particularly to children whom the industry targeted with s featuring cartoon characters, the most famous of which was known as “Joe Camel.”

Jury selection begins today in Oakland, a short drive from San Francisco and opening statements are expected to begin August 18.

Meta was convicted on similar grounds in separate trials held in Los Angeles and New Mexico, with combined damages that approach $1 billion.

In Oakland, the states are demanding a long list of changes to Meta’s apps, in addition to financial penalties as high as $1.4 trillion, close to Meta’s entire market value which hovers around $1.5 trillion.

Despite the eye-popping number, money isn’t Meta’s biggest problem, if it were to lose the case.

“The huge issue here is reputational harm” and being forced to make major changes, Joralemon said.

“Putting a CEO on the witness stand can be quite damning,” as well, he said.

Meta founder and chief Mark Zuckerberg is among the star witnesses expected to testify.

The case could be “the beginning of a broader reckoning” for Meta, Nora Freeman Engstrom told AFP via email. She is a law professor and associate dean at Stanford.

It will be important to see the “gap” between what Meta knew privately and what it disclosed publicly, Engstrom said.

Meta is “confident in our record of protecting teens online and will continue to defend ourselves against claims that misrepresent the facts,” Meta told AFP last week.

With so many plaintiffs suing Meta and other social media companies, these lawsuits could potentially “go on for decades,” Joralemon said.

In May, Snap, TikTok, YouTube and Meta settled with a school district in Kentucky for $27 million to avoid another trial that was expected to set a precedent for around 1,200 similar lawsuits.

On Monday, a federal appeals court ruled that more than 3,000 additional lawsuits filed against Meta, YouTube-parent Google, Snap and TikTok can proceed.

World.title: Colombia rescuers find woman alive as quake death toll passes 240
World.content:
Pereira – Colombian rescuers pulled a 32-year-old woman alive from the rubble of a collapsed building Tuesday, sparking cheers and applause as exhausted crews raced to find more survivors from the country’s strongest earthquake in a century.

Daniela Largo was carried from the wreckage wrapped in a blue blanket as rescuers embraced and relatives shouted out with joy.

The rescue came as soldiers, firefighters and volunteers searched collapsed buildings across western Colombia after a 7.4-magnitude quake killed at least 241 people and injured more than 1,600.

“We were losing hope and then we received a call,” said her mother Sandra Milena Perez in Pereira.

Perez said a local resident heard cries for help beneath the rubble and joined neighbors in removing debris before professional rescuers arrived.

“Thanks to him, today we’re happy,” she said. “At home her 12-year-old son is waiting for her.”

In Pereira and in Cali, emergency crews used cranes, dogs and heavy machinery to search ruined buildings while volunteers formed human chains to clear debris by hand, hoping to reach people still trapped beneath collapsed structures.

As darkness fell, families prepared to sleep in parks as aftershocks rattled damaged neighborhoods where entire blocks had been reduced to rubble.

The quake overwhelmed parts of the health system, turning the rescue effort into one of Colombia’s largest disaster responses in years.

“The house came down on top of us. I wasn’t able to get out,” said Beatriz Arcos, who was trapped with her husband and mother beneath their collapsed condominium.

“It took about an hour to get us out.” Arcos said she was hospitalized after a concrete block fell on her back. Her husband and mother were also injured.

In Cali, residents armed with picks, shovels and their bare hands joined firefighters in digging through collapsed buildings.

Rescuers stopped every few minutes to call into the rubble and listen for any response.

“We’re doing this with our hands, with gloves” said volunteer Pablo Cesar Ruiz “It’s sad to see time slipping away.”

In Pereira, army units and sniffer dogs combed through twisted concrete and exposed steel.

At one site, a rescue squad leader abruptly raised his fist, stopping workers so they could listen for signs of life.

Volunteers formed human chains, passing bricks and chunks of masonry hand-to-hand to clear paths into collapsed structures.

– ‘So much effort’ –

For many families, the desperate search was becoming a vigil.

“My aunt lived there. She’s under the rubble,” said Jorge Gonzalez, standing beside a collapsed building in Pereira.

“I arrived yesterday and I haven’t left, and until they find her body I don’t intend to leave here.”

While some families waited for news of missing relatives, others were grappling with the loss of homes, possessions and livelihoods.

“We lost everything,” said Stella Galvis, fighting back tears after escaping the collapse of her home.

“We survived by a miracle, since I managed to get my little boy out and my partner managed to get out too.”

From the air, neighborhoods in Cali appeared flattened, with piles of grey rubble replacing entire blocks of homes and apartment buildings.

Nearby, cars lay crushed beneath fallen walls and concrete slabs.

On one mound of debris, a young couple climbed over broken masonry searching for belongings.

They recovered a box from inside a child’s bright red bedside table.

Many survivors spent the night outdoors, either because their homes were damaged or because they feared aftershocks.

One park in Pereira was transformed into a makeshift shelter with tents and mattresses.

“We lost everything, but we’re alive,” said 23-year-old John Tabasco, who was camped there with his wife and seven-month-old son.

“We’ve never had to do this before, to depend on someone else to help us. It’s amazing how life can change.”

Others struggled to come to terms with losing homes built over decades.

“You buy a little house with so much effort, spending 40, 50 years struggling to get yourself that house, you finally get it and in just a few days it all goes down the drain,” said 79-year-old Jaime Alzate.

In Cali, part of the Hospital Universitario del Valle collapsed during the quake, forcing doctors to move patients into a parking lot and treat some in the open air.

Yet amid the destruction, many Colombians mobilized to help.

Thousands brought water, food and supplies to affected neighborhoods, while long lines formed outside blood donation centers.

“It’s about wanting to help your community, your city and your country,” said blood donor Ferney Cabrera.

President Abelardo de la Espriella declared a state of emergency and promised rent subsidies for affected families Tuesday during a visit to Pereira.

The United States announced $15.5 million in emergency aid, while messages of support and offers of assistance arrived from around the world.

As aftershocks continued to rattle damaged cities, rescue crews pressed on through the ruins, hoping more voices, taps or whistles might still emerge.

World.title: Passengers rescued as second ferry in days catches fire in Indonesia
World.content:
Mataram – A navy vessel and other ships rushed in Wednesday to rescue over 100 people from a ferry on fire off the tourist island of Bali, officials said, in the second such incident in days.

There were no immediate reports of casualties among the passengers and crew, with at least 114 people on board, according to the manifest.

The passenger ferry had been sailing from Bali to the next-door island of Lombok when it caught fire in the early morning hours.

Muhamad Hariyadi, head of the search and rescue agency at Mataram on Lombok island, said the total number of passengers on board was being verified.

He said passengers were evacuated on at least three different vessels, including a navy ship and another ferry.

Search and rescue vessels were at the scene and a helicopter was conducting surveillance from the air.

“As of now, we have not received any report of casualties,” Hariyadi told Metro TV.

“We have approached the ship and confirmed that all passengers are no longer on board,” he added. “We visually see no passengers on the ship.”

Last week, five people died when a ferry caught fire off Java island.

Marine accidents are a regular occurrence in Indonesia — an archipelago of more than 17,000 islands that rely heavily on boat connections.

Lax safety standards and unpredictable weather are the main reasons for the disasters.

A ferry transporting more than 70 people sank while sailing near Selayar, a small island south of Sulawesi, last month.

Four bodies were recovered, but the search operation ended with 14 others still officially missing.

World.title: Charges dropped against Bondi Beach attack hero
World.content:
Sydney – Australian police dropped assault charges on Wednesday against a man lauded for his bravery during last year’s mass shooting at Bondi Beach.

Fruit seller Ahmed al Ahmed was hailed as a hero after footage showed him disarming a gunman during the December 14 attack, which killed 15 people at a Jewish festival.

Ahmed was earlier this year accused of stalking and assaulting his father, charges he denied.

Both charges were withdrawn after a brief hearing on Wednesday, court documents showed.

Ahmed ducked between parked cars as the Bondi shooting unfolded, grabbing one of the two gunmen and wresting away his weapon in an effort to stop the killing.

He sustained gunshot wounds in the attack.

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese would later meet Ahmed in person, describing him as a “true Australian hero” and an inspiration to all.

World.title: Oil prices rise, stocks mixed ahead of crucial US inflation data
World.content:
Hong Kong – Oil prices rose again Wednesday and stock markets were mixed, with eyes on the release of key US inflation data that could guide the Federal Reserve on its plans for interest rates.

Traders trod nervously ahead of the consumer price index (CPI) figures, which follow a report last week showing the world’s top economy lost more than 20,000 jobs last month, suggesting the labour market was slackening.

With inflation stubbornly elevated above the Fed’s two percent target for more than five years — compounded by the Iran war since February — monetary policymakers are increasingly considering lifting borrowing costs.

The bank’s July meeting saw three board members call for an increase, dissenting from the final decision to hold rates, and investors are betting they will announce one before the end of the year, with some eyeing at least two.

Analysts pointed out that there will be one more CPI release and another jobs report before the Fed’s next meeting in September.

The higher oil prices rise, the more traders expect the Fed to tighten, and a lack of progress in talks between the US and Iran on a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz is adding upward momentum.

An announcement from Pakistan’s defence minister that the two were “close to some sort of arrangement” provided a sliver of hope Tuesday, though that later faded.

His remarks came after Washington and Tehran had issued demands for compensation over the five-month war, hardening their positions.

Meanwhile, a US helicopter fired missiles on Tuesday into the engine room of a Panama-flagged cargo ship that attempted to break the American blockade of Iran’s ports, the United States military said.

There was also little major reaction to a report that Iran and Oman were in advanced talks on reopening Hormuz to some maritime shipping.

Both main crude contracts rose Wednesday, and have risen around 14 percent in the past week.

“Crude oil prices have surged in the last few days because the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively shut, and there are no signs of progress between the US and Iran,” wrote Forex.com’s Fawad Razaqzada.

“The latest headlines around talks between Oman and Iran provided some relief, but we shouldn’t confuse talks with an actual breakthrough. Iran has come out saying that the Strait of Hormuz will remain shut until their conditions are met.”

He said the positions of the US and Iran indicated “any potential deal is still some way off, meaning risks remain skewed to the upside for oil prices”.

Equity markets fluctuated ahead of the CPI release, though Seoul enjoyed another strong day as it claws back some of the huge tech-led losses sustained in July.

The Kospi climbed more than three percent, helped by chipmakers SK hynix and Samsung, which bore the brunt of that selloff.

The gains were helped by strong earnings reports from US AI giants CoreWeave and Super Micro Computer that eased worries about the years-long investment boom that has led many observers to question when firms will see a return.

Tokyo, Shanghai, Taipei, Manila and Jakarta also rose, though Hong Kong, Sydney, Singapore and Wellington were in the red.

World.title: How difficult is it to become a doctor or an engineer in India?
World.content:
For a very long time, anyone considered particularly good at studies in India was almost automatically tipped to become a doctor or an engineer.

3 Idiots

made a joke of that national fixation years ago, showing a world in which parents and professors seemed convinced they knew what success ought to look like.

Alternative streams of education have slowly gained popularity since then. The race to become a doctor or engineer, however, has hardly become easier. As the pool of aspirants expands beyond the metros, competition for a coveted seat has only become harder. Many tuition centres, almost like factories, in Kota and other places train students rigorously to pass these coveted exams.

The May 3 NEET-UG examination was cancelled after the paper-leak controversy and nearly 20 lakh candidates returned for a re-examination on June 21. The anger travelled from coaching rooms to Ja

r Mantar and towards Parliament, propelled by the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party.

Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as education minister on July 25. The CBI chargesheet has since named 13 accused, including three subject experts associated with NTA, while CJP has demanded that the testing agency itself be replaced. Similar protests over exam leaks have now erupted in Jharkhand.

The anger that erupted at Jantar Mantar after the leak is merely a reflection of the deeper anxiety over competition for quality jobs and the yearning for a stronger CV, which for many begins with studying at a hallowed institution. How difficult, then, is it to get into a top-tier engineering or medical college in India?

The IIT-NIT funnel

Engineering here means the route to the country's most sought-after public engineering institutions, particularly the IITs and NITs, not every engineering college.





The pathways are slightly different. JEE Main is the direct gateway to the 31 NITs participating in JoSAA 2026, while it also acts as the screening stage for candidates hoping to reach the IITs through JEE Advanced.

NTA recorded 15,38,468 unique candidates appearing for JEE Main 2026. Of the 1,87,389 who registered for JEE Advanced, 1,79,694 appeared in both papers and 56,880 qualified. The JoSAA 2026 matrix provides 18,826

seats.

Put another way, the original Main candidate pool is roughly 82 times the number of IIT seats. Even after reaching JEE Advanced, there were 9.5 test-takers and almost exactly three qualifiers for every IIT place.

How competitive is the field

Not every JEE Main candidate is a serious IIT contender, so the 82-to-one comparison is largely academic. It is a measure of the scale of the field, not an individual's admission probability. Seats are allocated across categories and other reservation rules.

But in both IITs and NITs, the fight is not only for a seat, but also for a preferred stream and college.

Interest in admission wanes considerably as one goes down the value chain. That distinction becomes clearer when one looks at the rest of India's engineering system. The latest Rajya Sabha disclosure by the ministry states that BTech/BE enrolment in AICTE-approved institutions rose to 13.56 lakh in 2025-26. Yet adding up the state-wise vacancies in the same annexure produces 2,52,914 empty seats.

In the same year, 67 AICTE-approved engineering and technology institutions applied for closure or were listed as closed.

So India does not lack engineering seats. What it lacks are the seats students value most in IITs, top NITs and other highly sought-after institutions.

What government told in Parliament

The engineering race does not necessarily end with a BTech for all. For those aiming for an MTech from an IIT, NIT or another premier institution, GATE becomes another competitive gate.

The numbers are substantial. In GATE 2026, 2,11,020 candidates appeared for the Computer Science and Information Technology paper, while 95,752 appeared for Electronics and Communication, 76,385 for Civil Engineering and 69,242 for Data Science and Artificial Intelligence.

Those figures cannot simply be converted into applicants-per-MTech-seat ratios. Candidates can sit more than one GATE paper. For NITs, the pool is still broader.

CCMT 2026 accepts valid GATE scores from 2024, 2025 and 2026. So candidates for these seats can effectively be competing with more than one year's GATE cohort. However, suffice to say, the odds are tough for aspirants.

Medicine has its own hierarchy

Medical education runs on the same preference for high-value seats. For the valid June 21 NEET re-examination, 22,79,743 candidates were registered, 19,99,895 appeared and 11,21,185 qualified. The cancellation itself affected the denominator, with 2,79,848 registered candidates not sitting the re-test.

Against this pool, the NMC's July matrix lists 1,36,939 MBBS seats for 2026-27, excluding Institutes of National Importance such as AIIMS. The NEET test-taker pool is about 14.6 times the listed MBBS capacity, while the number of qualified candidates is about 8.2 times the capacity. These are broad national comparisons, not individual admission odds, since seats are divided across quotas, categories and state eligibility rules.

But the headline number conceals another hierarchy.

Of those 1,36,939 NMC-listed seats, 63,296 are in government colleges and 73,643 are private. Private colleges account for about 54% of the listed capacity. If we compare the NEET re-test pool only with NMC-listed government seats, the candidate pool is roughly 31.6 times the available government capacity.

Level of competition

Government seats are prized because of substantially greater affordability, the reputation of established institutions and, in many large public hospitals, the prospect of extensive clinical exposure.

This year's expansion makes that distinction sharper. NMC approved 9,911 additional MBBS seats for 2026-27. Of these, 7,800 are private and only 2,111 government.

Skewed nature of growth of MBBA seats

Nearly four out of every five newly approved seats were added on the private side. So medicine and engineering are more alike than they look. In both, the real contest is increasingly over which seat, in which institution, and at what cost. There is, however, an important difference between the engineering and medical journeys.

An engineer can enter another fierce competition through GATE for MTech, but postgraduate study remains an optional route for most. For doctors who want to specialise, postgraduate training is much closer to another necessary career gate.

The latest completed NEET-PG examination makes the scale clear. More than 2.42 lakh candidates appeared for NEET-PG 2025, according to the National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences.

NEET-PG 2026 is yet to be held and is scheduled for August 30.

And the postgraduate pool is much smaller than the undergraduate universe. The Centre said in July that India had 86,360 postgraduate medical seats in 2025-26. Earlier this year, it said 8,967 additional PG seats, including those in AIIMS and other Institutes of National Importance, had been approved for 2025-26. For some who pursue super-specialisation, there may still be another competitive gate beyond that.

Governments have tried to build capacity

Governments have tried to accommodate more students in quality institutions. Seven IITs have been established since 2014, while approved expansion at five newer IITs is intended to create capacity for another 6,500 students. In medicine, 157 government medical colleges have been approved under one central scheme, with 137 already functional. Separate government programmes have also expanded undergraduate and postgraduate capacity.

But adding seats does not automatically solve the problem. The latest figures placed before Parliament show 15.35 lakh registered allopathic doctors and 7.52 lakh AYUSH practitioners and, assuming 80% availability in both groups, a government-estimated combined practitioner-population ratio of 1:778. Yet the existence of incentives for hard-to-serve areas underlines another problem. Doctors and specialists are not distributed evenly.

So hierarchy exists beyond educational institutions too, which makes the work of policymakers even harder in a large country like India.

How other countries filter their best

In the US, 54,699 people applied to MD-granting medical schools in 2025 and 23,440 matriculated, but candidates generally apply after or during undergraduate study and typically take the MCAT. In England, medicine remains one of the most competitive university routes, with a sizeable socioeconomic gap in acceptance rates.

France pushes much of the filter inside university, with two in five students entering its PASS or L.AS health routes in 2022 reaching medicine or another major health discipline within two years. China's Gaokao had 1.29 crore registrations in 2026, but admissions are distributed across provinces, universities and programmes rather than through a single NEET-style medicine pool. Russia uses another lever altogether, with targeted state-funded medical training linked to future employment and workforce.

Every country has tried different approaches based on the reality of the land. Whether a test like NEET is the best way forward is still being intensely debated. However, for policymakers, the only feasible solution seems to be building more institutions of comparable quality, ones students believe can offer strong education, credible employment prospects and a better quality of life. Simply multiplying seats is unlikely to be enough if aspirants continue to see only a small proportion of them as worth fighting for.

World.title: Lok Sabha inquiry panel  indicts ex-HC judge Yashwant Varma in cash-at-home case
World.content:
The panel found Justice Varmaâs explanation over the discovery of unaccounted cash at his official residence "evasive" and "unsatisfactory".

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A Lok Sabha inquiry committee on Wednesday indicted former Allahabad High Court judge Yashwant Varma in the cash-at-home case.The panel found Justice Varmaâs explanation for the discovery of unaccounted cash at his official residence "evasive" and "unsatisfactory". Its report, tabled in both Houses of Parliament, said all three charges against Varma were proved.The committee said the charges are threefold - firstly, discovery and possession of unexplained Indian currency notes within official premises; secondly, failure to preserve and causing interference with material evidence; and thirdly, furnishing evasive and misleading explanations.The committee examined documentary and electronic material and recorded evidence from witnesses. It also noted that Varma was given an opportunity to respond to the charges and present his defence."The statement of grounds accompanying the charges records the occurrence of fire, discovery of cash, location of the storeroom within the Government-allotted residence, the alleged conduct after the fire, and the explanation offered by the Judge," the inquiry report said."Article I is proved. Substantial unexplained Rs 500 denomination currency notes were found in the storeroom situated within the official residential premises at 30, Tughlaq Crescent, New Delhi.The Judge failed to furnish a satisfactory explanation regarding the presence, source or ownership thereof," it said.On the third charge, the committee said Varmaâs explanation, including his March 22, 2025 response and subsequent statements, did not demonstrate the "candour, transparency and institutional responsibility" expected in the circumstances. It remained evasive and unsatisfactory when tested against evidence from independent officials and other corroborative material.A large amount of unaccounted, partially burnt cash was discovered in the outhouse of Varmaâs official residence following a fire in March 2025. The discovery triggered allegations of judicial corruption, which Varma denied.Following an in-house inquiry ordered by the then Chief Justice of India, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla constituted a three-member panel headed by Supreme Court judge Aravind Kumar under the Judges (Inquiry) Act. The motion for the inquiry was backed by MPs from different political parties.Varma resigned during the inquiry. It remains unclear whether Parliament will proceed with the committeeâs findings, as some legal experts have argued that the Judges (Inquiry) Act can be invoked only against a serving judge.

World.title: 'No force used': Cong defends J'khand govt amid youth stir, accuses BJP of shielding ‘exam mafia’
World.content:
Congress on Wednesday defended the Jharkhand governmentâs handling of the studentsâ agitation over alleged examination irregularities, claiming that no force was used against protesting students and accusing the BJP of attempting to divert the issue.

The Congress ministers said the state government had taken steps to check examination paper leaks even before the students took to the streets. They alleged that the BJP, instead of supporting an investigation by the Jharkhand CID, was demanding a CBI probe to âshield the exam mafiaâ, news agency PTI reports.

"To shield 'exam mafia', BJP wants probe into paper leaks by its 'tool' CBI instead of Jharkhand CID."

The Congress leaders also accused the BJP of adopting a different approach when it was in power in Jharkhand, alleging that the previous BJP government had âcrushed the voice of youthâ during protests.

Cong claims 152 paper leaks since 2015 under BJP

Citing party data, the ministers claimed that 152 paper leaks had been reported across the country since 2015 under BJP rule, but the CBI had investigated only 17 of these cases and there had been no convictions.

The Congress ministers further alleged that the BJP's Jharkhand leadership was acting at the Centre's behest to disrupt the students' agitation. They claimed that gheraoing the state assembly was not part of the protesters' original agenda and alleged that the BJP brought people from other states to disrupt the students' âpeacefulâ protest in Ranchi on August 10.

World.title: 'Allocate time starting today': Shah writes to LS Speaker for debate on NEET protest by students
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Union home minister

on Wednesday wrote a letter to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla and asked him to allocate time for a discussion over the student protest on NEET paper leak.

In the letter, Shah said that the Lower House already discussed the Public Examination (prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, claiming that none of the opposition MPs expressed their views.

"As you are aware, Honâble parliamentary affairs minister Shri Kiren Rijiju has agreed, on behalf of the government, to a discussion in Parliament on the student movement concerning the NEET examination, during the meeting of the Business Advisory Committee," Shah said.

"I would also like to mention that even before the opposition made this request, the Lok Sabha had already discussed the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 during the ongoing session.

However, none of the Honâble opposition MPs expressed any views in the House regarding the NEET examination during that discussion. Despite this, the government is once again ready for a discussion on the issue," he added.

Shah said that solution emerge through discussion and dialogue and urged the Speaker to consult the leaders of the opposition and facilitate a discussion on the issue.

"I request you to consult the opposition and, through mutual consensus, kindly allocate as much time as you deem appropriate, for as many hours as considered suitable, starting today.





I wish to remain present in the House during the allotted time, participate in the discussion on this issue, and am prepared to answer all questions raised by the opposition," the letter reads.

"In a democracy, solutions emerge through discussion and dialogue. I have unwavering faith in democracy and democratic institutions, and I believe that this House exists precisely for discussion and dialogue. Therefore, I urge you to consult the leaders of the opposition and facilitate a discussion on this important issue in a conducive atmosphere, so that all Honâble members from both the treasury and opposition benches can present their valuable views and opinions on the matter," he added.

Shah's letter came amid opposition protests demanding, him to make a statement in Parliament on the alleged police brutality against student protesters on July 20.

Earlier in the day, Shah offered to sit in the Parliament to hear the opposition's concerns and respond to every point, amid protests over his "absence" from the Houses.

Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, however rejected the offer saying they "seeks answers, not lectures."

"The opposition has clearly said that we are not interested in Amit Shah giving us a lecture. When I say 'we', I mean the younger generation of this country. Who shot the students? Who gave the order to beat up the students with lathis with nails? Did Amit Shah give this order to shoot our children? If he did, then he should resign. For the last 20 days, Amit Shah has been missing. The Home Minister of India has no courage; he cannot come to the House," Rahul said.

World.title: FCRA Bill sent to Joint Parliamentary Committee amid opposition ruckus
World.content:
FCRA amendment bill sent to JPC (Image: IANS)

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA) Amendment Bill was formally referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) on Wednesday after the Centre moved a motion to this effect in Parliament.Union minister Nityanand Rai moved the motion in the Lok Sabha after the House resumed proceedings following its morning adjournment."That the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, be referred to a Joint Committee of the Houses consisting of 21 Members of this House to be nominated by the Hon'ble Speaker, Lok Sabha, and 10 members of Rajya Sabha to be nominated by Hon'ble Chairman, Rajya Sabha," the motion moved by the junior home minister stated.According to the Supplementary List of Business for the Lok Sabha, the proposed Joint Committee will comprise 31 members, including 21 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha.The committee will examine the Bill in detail and submit its report to Parliament by the last day of the first week of the Winter Session in 2026.The motion also specified that one-third of the committeeâs total membership would constitute the quorum for its meetings.While the government has moved to refer the Bill to a committee for review, the Congress has maintained its opposition to the legislation and called for its complete withdrawal. The Opposition has previously raised concerns that the proposed amendments could be used to target civil society and minority institutions.Congress MP KC Venugopal sought the withdrawal of the Bill, a demand that also received support from Samajwadi Party MP Akhilesh Yadav.In reply, parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said the opposition should welcome the government's decision to refer the Bill to a JPC, adding that it contained no provision targeting minority institutions.The FCRA regulates the receipt and use of foreign contributions by individuals, associations and organisations in India, with the aim of ensuring that such funds are used for the purposes for which they are received.The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, was introduced in the Lok Sabha on March 25 and is currently under consideration by Parliament.The monsoon session of Parliament began on July 20 and is scheduled to conclude on August 13. Proceedings have been repeatedly disrupted by opposition protests over several issues, including Delhi Police action against protesters on July 20. Several Bills have been passed in the Lok Sabha amid opposition protests and limited debate.

World.title: How Corporate India Is Investing In Climate & Environmental Resilience
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

For years, environmental CSR in India was largely associated with tree plantation drives, cleanliness campaigns and occasional conservation projects. While those initiatives continue, companies are increasingly directing their CSR efforts towards something far more strategic. Theyâre strengthening climate resilience, securing water resources, promoting circular use of materials, and helping communities adapt to a warming world.The change reflects a growing realisation that environmental sustainability is no longer just about protecting nature. It is about protecting livelihoods, businesses, and the economy itself.Climate change is already affecting water availability, agriculture, supply chains, and industrial operations. As these risks intensify, Corporate India is beginning to see environmental CSR not as philanthropy but as an investment in long-term resilience.The scale of the challenge is enormous. India's draft Climate Finance Taxonomy estimates that the country will require around $2.5 trillion (Roughly an estimated Rs 2,50,00,000 crore or Rs 250 trillion) to meet its climate commitments by 2030, while climate adaptation alone could require investments of nearly Rs 56.7 trillion during the same period.These figures underline why resilience has become a business imperative as much as an environmental one.Increasingly, companies are aligning their CSR programmes with this new reality. Water has emerged as one of the biggest priorities.According to the Central Ground Water Board, India extracts 245.6 billion cubic metres (BCM) of groundwater annually, with 751 assessment units already categorised as over-exploited, 206 as critical and another 711 as semi-critical. Agriculture accounts for 87% of groundwater extraction, making water scarcity a concern that extends far beyond farms to industries, cities and supply chains.For CSR programmes, this has meant a shift from isolated water projects towards landscape-level interventions. Infosys, for instance, reports creating 40 lakes across its campuses with a combined rainwater storage capacity of 430 million litres, supported by 409 deep injection wells and complete recycling of wastewater.UltraTech Cement says its operations became 4.9 times water positive during FY2024-25 through rainwater harvesting, groundwater recharge, watershed management and recycling initiatives. Hindustan Zinc reports achieving 3.3 times water positivity while targeting a 50% reduction in freshwater consumption by 2030. ITC, meanwhile, has expanded watershed restoration and river basin stewardship programmes alongside improvements in water-use efficiency.The common thread running through these initiatives is that they benefit both communities and businesses. Restoring watersheds improves groundwater availability for nearby villages while also reducing water-related risks for industrial operations. Wastewater recycling lowers pressure on freshwater resources while helping industries operate more sustainably.The focus is also widening beyond water. Another emerging area for CSR is the circular economy, where companies seek to minimise waste and maximise the productive use of resources. Rather than viewing waste simply as something to be disposed of, businesses are increasingly investing in recycling, reuse and resource recovery.India's policy framework now covers plastics, batteries, e-waste, waste tyres, construction waste and several other waste streams under Extended Producer Responsibility rules. As of March 2026, registered recyclers had processed 417.6 lakh metric tonnes of waste, generating nearly 342 lakh metric tonnes of EPR certificates. The government has also introduced a Rs 1,500 crore incentive scheme to promote recycling of critical minerals such as lithium, nickel and cobalt.Corporate initiatives are increasingly reflecting this transition. Tata Steel reported recycling around 4.2 million tonnes of scrap during FY2024-25. Infosys diverted 98% of its waste away from landfills, while Hindustan Zinc is working towards achieving near-zero waste to landfill by 2030 through greater reuse and recycling. These examples demonstrate how environmental investments can reduce raw material consumption, lower disposal costs, and improve resource security.CSR is also beginning to support innovation rather than only funding conventional projects. Technology-led solutions are emerging as an important area of investment. Digital Paani, featured in NITI Aayog's Frontier Tech Repository, uses Internet of Things-based automation to optimise wastewater treatment plants. The platform has been deployed at more than 40 facilities, treating over 90 million litres of wastewater every day.In agriculture, Kheyti's "greenhouse-in-a-box" model has demonstrated how climate-smart farming can improve resilience. According to the study cited in the report, participating farmers recorded a 73% increase in income, 58% lower crop losses, 67% lower water consumption, and significantly lower fertiliser use. Satellite-enabled platforms such as SatSure are also helping govts, financial institutions and agribusinesses assess climate risks and improve decision-making using artificial intelligence and Earth observation data.The evolution of environmental CSR reflects a broader shift in corporate thinking. Earlier, environmental spending was often evaluated through the number of trees planted or awareness campaigns organised.Today, companies are increasingly asking whether their investments improve water security, strengthen ecosystems, reduce resource consumption, and help communities withstand climate shocks.The approach also aligns more closely with business priorities. Healthier watersheds mean more reliable water supplies. Circular resource use reduces dependence on virgin materials. Climate-resilient agriculture strengthens rural livelihoods while improving supply-chain stability. Investments in environmental resilience, therefore, generate benefits that extend beyond compliance or corporate reputation.

World.title: BJP politicising Jharkhand students’ stir, brought people from other States to disrupt protests: Congress
World.content:
The Congress on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) hit out at the BJP, accusing it of "politicising" the students’ exam agitation in Jharkhand and “bringing people from other states” to disrupt the protests.

Accusing the saffron party of being involved in "exam mafia" across the country, the Congress said the BJP was “opposing” the CID probe into paper leaks in the state, “fearing that it would get exposed”.

A probe by the CBI, “a tool of the Centre”, will yield the “desired results” for them even in Jharkhand, asserted four Congress Ministers – Radha Krishna Kishore, Shilpy Neha Tirkey, Dipika Pandey Singh and Irfan Ansari – at a press conference Ranchi.

“The BJP brought people from other States to disrupt the students' peaceful protest in Ranchi on August 10 over exam irregularities. We urge Chief Minister Hemant Soren to ensure that each such BJP worker is identified and strong action is taken against them,” Mr. Kishore said.

He alleged that the BJP’s state leadership acted at the Centre's behest to disrupt the students' stir, as the recent assembly gherao in Ranchi was "not on the protesters' agenda".

Claiming that the Jharkhand government initiated steps in exam “anomalies” much before the students started their protests, Mr. Singh said, “152 paper leaks took place in the country since 2015 under the BJP rule, but CBI probe was conducted in only 17 such cases with zero conviction”.

Mr. Singh said the CBI probes included the NEET-UG 2024, UGC-NET 2024, SSC-CGL 2017, JEE Main 2021 and the West Bengal SSC 2016, “but the outcome was nothing”.

Regarding the Haryana Judicial Services 2017 case, a conviction was secured not by the CBI, but by an SIT constituted by the state authorities, she claimed.

Ms. Tirkey asserted that no force was used on the protesting students in Jharkhand, whereas during the earlier BJP regime in the state, “the voice of the youth was crushed”.

She also said that it was Congress leader Rahul Gandhi who worked to awaken the youth across the country through the ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ campaign.

This awareness is now giving students the courage to step forward and participate in these movements, asserted Ms. Tirkey.

“Even at Jantar Mantar during the NEET protests, Rahul Gandhi was present to boost the morale and courage of the students,” she said.

World.title: Tata Sons chairman N. Chandrasekaran to step down in February 2027
World.content:
Tata Sons chairman N. Chandrasekharan announced he would step down at the end of his tenure in February 2027, with no clarity emerging on his reappointment as chair of the Tata Group holding company.

“Earlier today, I have communicated to the Tata Sons Board, that I have decided not to offer myself for reappointment when my term ends on February 20, 2027. I have asked the Board to decide on the succession soon to ensure a proper transition,” Mr. Chandrasekaran said in a statement.

Stating that he had completed 40 years of professional life at the Tata Group, he said he was grateful for the immensely satisfying opportunity to contribute to this venerable institution.

“Leading Tata Sons over the past decade has been a great honour and a profound responsibility,” he said.

“My current tenure as the chairman of Tata Sons comes to an end on February 20, 2027. Sir Dorabji Tata Trust and Sir Ratan Tata Trust had unanimously resolved and recommended the extension of my next term for a period of five years, which was recorded and recommended by the Tata Sons Nomination and Remuneration Committee and the Board,” the chairman said in the statement.

“Subsequently, the resolution was tabled in the Tata Sons Board on February 24, 2026. However, the proposal was not carried through because one of the Board Members did not support it, and in the absence of unanimous support, I chose to defer the decision,” he said.

Though Mr. Chandrasekaran did not name the dissenting Board member in his statement, it is learnt that Tata Trusts chairman and Tata Sons Board member Noel Tata had not cleared his reappointment.

“It has been six months since that Board meeting, and no resolution has been reached till date. Tata Sons is a very large institution and there are many strategic projects that are under critical stages of execution,” he stated.

“It is not only necessary to have a leader in place to lead the Group beyond Feb 2027, but also clarity on leadership is important for employees, investors, partners and other stakeholders,” he said, adding that under these circumstances, earlier today, he had communicated to the Board not to continue beyond the end of his tenure.

Mr. Chandrasekaran, who had joined the Tata Sons board in October 2016, was designated chairman in January 2017 and took official charge in February 2017 in the aftermath of the sacking of Cyrus Mistry as chairman of Tata Sons.

Tata Group ​stocks fell up to 4% on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) after Mr. Chandrasekharan’s announcement ‌sparked a ‌selloff ⁠across the conglomerate’s ⁠listed companies. India’s top IT services ​exporter, Tata ‌Consultancy Services (TCS), led the losses, sliding 4.1%, ‌while Jaguar ​Land Rover-parent Tata Motors PV ⁠fell 2.8%.

(With inputs from Reuters)

World.title: Former Chinese Premier Zhu Rongji dies of illness at 98
World.content:
Former Chinese Premier Zhu Rongji has died, according to state media. The impatient, sharp-tongued reformer helped ignite China's explosive economic boom by forcing wrenching change on state industry in the 1990s and leading the country into the World Trade Organisation.

Also read: In China’s parliament, a long list of millionaires

The official Xinhua news agency reported that Mr. Zhu died of illness in Beijing at around 11 a.m. on Wednesday (August 12, 2026). He was 97 years old.

Once sent into rural exile to do manual labour for praising reforms in other communist countries, Mr. Zhu pushed through a dizzying array of changes as premier, China's top economic post, from 1998 to 2003.

Mr. Zhu clashed with Communist Party conservatives and state industry bosses as he pushed state-owned companies to become efficient and profitable. That cost millions of layoffs, but helped propel China to overtake Japan as the second-largest economy behind the United States in 2010.

Building on former leader Deng Xiaoping's 1979 reforms, Mr. Zhu is credited with supplying the resourcefulness and tenacity to push through history-making changes such as China's WTO membership, which helped to transform China into the world's biggest exporter.

Those changes helped to keep economic growth above 8% a year from 2000-2010, peaking at 14.2% in 2007.

Named premier in 1998 at age 69, Mr. Zhu became a popular figure by criticising official bungling and graft and accepting blame when the government fell short. His demanding style earned him the nicknames Boss and Zhu Fengzi, or Madman Zhu.

“I have prepared 100 coffins here — 99 for corrupt officials and one for myself,” Mr. Zhu said in 1998, according to the party newspaper People's Daily.

Mr. Zhu ranked No. 3 in the party hierarchy behind President Jiang Zemin and Li Peng, chairman of the ceremonial legislature, the National People's Congress. But he was a technician without his own power base. Mr. Zhu complained that allowed officials to ignore his orders.

Mr. Zhu made his name as a deputy premier in the 1990s by crushing inflation. He enforced price controls and cut off loans to money-losing state companies, rebuffing resistance by local leaders — a pattern Mr. Zhu would repeat as he fought conservatives over the pace of reform.

Mr. Zhu led efforts to secure WTO membership following marathon negotiations that began in the 1980s. That status would enshrine free trade as a national commitment, giving Zhu a tool to force local officials to stop protecting favored companies.

His campaign was nearly derailed when he went to Washington in 1999 with market-opening concessions to win U.S. endorsement of the WTO bid.

The Clinton administration rejected the offer as inadequate while his political enemies at home accused him of offering too much, but Mr. Zhu survived and China went on to join the body in December 2001.

Mr. Zhu launched China's home ownership boom in 1998 with an initiative to sell apartments owned by state companies. Families rushed to buy, and within a decade the majority of urban housing was privately owned.

Still, Mr. Zhu was less an advocate of free enterprise than a skilled bureaucrat who carried out party orders to whip state industry into shape.

Mr. Zhu showed no interest in privatizing the economy. He played a key role in drafting plans in the 1990s to turn banks, airlines, oil companies and other enterprises into profit-oriented corporations but to retain government ownership.

Born Oct 23, 1928, in Mao Zedong's home province of Hunan, Mr. Zhu paid an early price for his willingness to take risks and speak out.

After a start as an economic planner, his career went into a 22-year eclipse when he was labelled a “rightist” in 1957 for praising reforms in Hungary and Yugoslavia. He was banished to the countryside during the 1966-76 Cultural Revolution to do manual labor.

Rehabilitated in 1979, Mr. Zhu rose swiftly, becoming deputy Shanghai party secretary in 1987 and mayor the next year.

As mayor in 1989, Mr. Zhu gained a reputation for moderation when he placated protesters and pledged not to call in the military.

“He managed to defuse, with considerable subtlety, a tense political situation that could have developed into localized violence or worse if the military had felt it necessary to intervene,” wrote Australian diplomat Shelley Warner in the 1991 book “The Pro-Democracy Protests in China: Reports from the Provinces.”

Mr. Zhu's boss, Jiang, would soon be called to Beijing by Deng and made party leader. Zhu was named deputy premier in 1991 and joined the party's ruling Standing Committee in 1993.

Mr. Zhu broke with the leadership's stance of infallibility by admitting and taking blame for official failings.

In 1998, after summer floods killed 4,150 people and officials were accused of embezzling money meant for anti-flood dikes, Mr. Zhu complained some barriers were no stronger than bean curd.

Three years later, he apologized on national television for his Cabinet's failure to protect the public after an explosion in a schoolhouse in southern China killed at least 42 people, most of them children.

Mr. Zhu enlivened the party's bland image by cracking jokes in public, sometimes at his own expense. Laughter erupted at a 1999 news conference when he said a recent photo “made me look like a dead man”.

One of Mr. Zhu's proudest triumphs as deputy premier was to craft a tax system that required local officials to hand more revenue to Beijing. He said in 1996 that he deserved a Nobel Prize in economics for that.

He rarely appeared in public after leaving office as premier.

World.title: Parliament Monsoon Session Day 18 LIVE: Rijiju says can extend session if Congress agrees for discussion on students' protests; LS adjourned for the day
World.content:
Amid massive Opposition furore, the Lok Sabha on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) adopted a motion to send the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, to a Joint Parliamentary Committee via voice vote. The House was adjourned for the day shortly after. Meanwhile, the Rajya Sabha passed the National Co-operative Development Corporation (Amendment) Bill, 2026, and took up the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026, for consideration and passing.

The adjournment till 11 a.m. on Thursday (August 13, 2026) came as the Opposition kept up with relentless protests even as the Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said Home Minister Amit Shah and the government are ready to immediately start a discussion in the Lok Sabha on the NEET-related students’ protests, provided the Opposition MPs maintain decorum and cooperates.

Also Read | Rajya Sabha passes Tribunals Reforms Bill in Opposition’s absence

Mr. Shah on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) wrote to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, asking him to consult with the Opposition on fixing the time and number of hours of the proposed discussion. Earlier in the day, the Home Minister, speaking to the reporters, said: “If Opposition gives it in writing to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla by 2 p.m. today, we can start a discussion at 3 p.m. today until 3 p.m. tomorrow. If the discussion starts, I will give a reply tomorrow at 3 p.m.” Hitting back, LoP Rahul Gandhi declines the offer, stating that the Opposition is “not interested” in Mr. Shah’s lecture.

Also Read | Lok Sabha passes Tribunals Reforms Bill amid din

The report of an inquiry committee which investigated allegations against Justice Yashwant Varma — against whom removal proceedings were initiated over the alleged discovery of unaccounted cash from his official residence — was tabled in Rajya Sabha. Rajya Sabha proceedings were adjourned in pre-lunch session without transacting any business following an uproar over BJP MP Sushmita Dev’s alleged derogatory remarks against CPM’s John Brittas.

World.title: Sri Lanka allows immigration clearance for refugees returning from India
World.content:
Colombo

Sri Lankan immigration authorities will henceforth allow refugees living in India to return to the island nation even if they had fled the war-torn country without a valid passport or through an unapproved port of departure.

The Sri Lanka Cabinet, which met on Monday (August 10, 2026), decided that the government would “facilitate clearance of immigration when the individuals who had left the country without using an approved port and a formal passport during the period of the war, sought refuge in India, but proved the nationality as Sri Lankan and returning to their motherland voluntarily”, according to a media statement following this week’s Cabinet decisions.

The decision assumes significance amid concerns raised by refugee rights activists over the detention of a few returnees last year. In May 2025, the arrest of a 75-year-old Sri Lankan Tamil refugee returning from India on charges of leaving the island without a valid passport drew attention. Sri Lankan authorities said they would address the issue. A total of 246 people from 46 families had returned from India to Sri Lanka between July 2025 and February 2026, with no arrests reported during the period, authorities subsequently pointed out.

However, to put in place formal procedures to facilitate the return of refugees, the government has now obtained instructions from the public prosecutor on immigration clearance. These include verification of the returnee’s identity, clearance from Sri Lanka’s State Intelligence Service, authentication of Sri Lankan nationality through Sri Lanka’s diplomatic missions in India for those displaced before August 1, 2006; and confirmation that the individuals have not committed murder, treason or any other offence prescribed under special provisions by law.

In March this year, Cabinet Minister and Leader of the House Bimal Rathnayake told The Hindu that Sri Lanka is ready to receive and support all those forced to flee the country during the civil war and now living as refugees in Tamil Nadu. He also urged the governments of India and Tamil Nadu to refrain from using refugees as “a tool for political propaganda”.

The Minister made the remarks in the context of former Tamil Nadu Chief Minister M.K. Stalin’s February 15, 2026, letter to Prime Minister Narendra Modi seeking the Union government’s intervention on issues facing Sri Lankan Tamils living in India for over four decades. According to the letter, around 89,000 refugees reside in and outside camps across Tamil Nadu, with nearly 40% of them having been born in India.

World.title: Commission to review 7.5% reservation for NEET-qualified govt. school students: Tamil Nadu Health Minister
World.content:
The Tamil Nadu government is set to review the existing 7.5% horizontal reservation for government school students in medical admissions. A commission headed by a retired judge will assess the reservation, including whether it should be increased or extended to allied health courses beyond MBBS/BDS.

At the launch of a National Deworming Day camp on Monday, Health Minister K.G. Arunraj was asked whether the existing 7.5% quota would be increased to 10% as per the recommendation of a Commission headed by Justice P. Kalaiyarasan, which was formed in 2020 by the then AIADMK government. Dr. Arunraj said it would be reviewed, and another commission was being constituted.

The Kalaiyarasan Commission was constituted to analyse the reasons for lower numbers of government school students getting admission to MBBS, and suggest remedial measures.

The new Commission will assess the extent to which the implementation of the reservation has benefited students, and determine how many more years the government should continue to implement it. The commission will also examine whether the 7.5% reservation should be extended to other allied health courses beyond MBBS/BDS, and whether the existing quota should be increased, the Minister said.

Merit list

Releasing the merit list for admission to MBBS/BDS for the academic year 2026-2027, the Minister said that counselling — offline for special category candidates and online for the general category — will begin on August 13.

The Tamil Nadu Selection Committee had received 41,726 applications for MBBS/BDS government quota seats, of which 35,926 were accepted. Under the 7.5% horizontal reservation for government school students, 4,860 applications were received, of which 3,625 were accepted. For management quota seats, a total of 30,907 applications were received, of which 26,956 were accepted.

A total of 468 applications were received for the sportspersons category, 524 in the children of ex-servicemen category, and 212 in the persons with benchmark disabilities category.

Dr. Arunraj said 9,999 MBBS seats would be filled through counselling this year.

While the State lost 800 MBBS seats after three private medical colleges obtained deemed university status, Tamil Nadu got an additional 850 MBBS seats this year - 150 in three government colleges and 700 in private colleges, he said.

He added that there were 2,000 BDS seats - 250 in government and remaining in private colleges.

A total of 537 MBBS seats and 104 BDS seats are available under the 7.5% reservation for government school students. Of the 537 MBBS seats, 335 are in government medical colleges and 202 in self-financing medical colleges. Of the 104 dental seats, 16 are in government and 88 in private dental colleges.

World.title: West Asia war LIVE: Iranian-backed Houthis kill 6 in attack on vessel
World.content:
Yemeni authorities said six people were killed by Iran-backed Houthi rebels attacking a vessel in the Bab el-Mandeb strait, while U.S. forces fired on a ship they said was trying to break a blockade of Iran’s ports.

Yemen’s coast guard said the dead included four crew members and two members of the government-allied National Resistance Forces. Houthis fired three ballistic missiles at the Yemeni commercial vessel, according to the Transportation Ministry of Yemen’s internationally recognised government. They are the first known deaths from Houthi attacks on shipping off Yemen in the latest bout of fighting in the Arab country.

Also read | Do not write the obituary of international law yet

Pakistan denounced on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) an attack by Houthi rebels on a vessel in the Red Sea in which three of its citizens were killed.

Also read | A new security triangle emerges with the Makkah Pact

Pakistan’s Interior Minister is visiting Iran to discuss regional security, stability and other developments, the foreign office said on Wednesday (August 12, 2026).

“He is discussing bilateral relations, security, regional security and stability, and constructive engagement amongst the parties in the region and regional developments,” Foreign Ministry spokesman Tahir Andrabi, whose government has been mediating to end the fighting in West Asia, told reporters in Islamabad.

The Lok Sabha on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) passed the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill 2026 without debate via a voice vote.
